the place it belongs to, as dragging the label sets it, in mm.

Limit.text: Limit is the dimension's limit: NoLimit, Minimum or Maximum.

Name.text: Name is what expressions read the constraint's value by, or "".

Other.text:
Other is whether an angle measures the supplementary angle, an
equal-angle constraint pairs the other angles, or a diameter is shown
as a radius.

Reference.text:
Reference reports whether the constraint is a reference dimension,
which measures and doesn't constrain.

Set.text:
Set gives the constraint a value, as editing its label on the
drawing does: a length in mm, an angle in degrees, a ratio. A
negative distance from a line or a plane puts the point on the
other side.

SetComment.text: SetComment changes the text of a comment.

SetExpr.text:
SetExpr gives the constraint the value of text, as typing it in its
label does: a length in the document's unit (View.Units), an angle in
degrees, a ratio. A plain number is stored as its value; any other
text, "25.4/2" or "wall*4" with a parameter (Params.Set), is
kept and evaluated again at each regeneration.

SetLabelOffset.text:
SetLabelOffset moves the label of a dimension or a comment to off
from the place it belongs to, as dragging it does. It changes how the
drawing looks, not what the sketch holds. For a comment off is where
the text stands, in the workplane it was written in.

SetLimit.text:
SetLimit makes the dimension a bound: Minimum lets what it measures
be its value or more, Maximum its value or less, and NoLimit makes it
hold its value again. Any distance, a diameter or radius, and an
angle take a limit; for an angle, Minimum is the least angle.

SetName.text:
SetName names the constraint, so that expressions read its value by
the name as they read a parameter: the value its label shows, in the
document's unit. Uses of an old name are renamed; "" takes the name
away, which a name in use can't be. A reference dimension can't be
named. Parameters and dimensions share the names.

SetOther.text:
SetOther makes an angle measure the supplementary angle, the other
one of the two its lines make, or not; for an equal-angle
constraint it pairs the other angles; a diameter is shown as a
radius, as the text window's "show as radius" does (ShowAsRadius).
Constrain > Other Supplementary Angle toggles it.

SetReference.text:
SetReference makes the constraint a reference dimension, or a
constraint again.

SetShowAsRadius.text:
SetShowAsRadius shows a diameter dimension as a radius, or as a
diameter again; the constraint holds the same size either way, and
Value is the one that is shown.

SetStyle.text:
SetStyle draws the constraint in the given style, as the window's
style list does for what is selected; the zero Style (api.Style{})
takes the style away, and the constraint is drawn in the constraint
style again. Only a comment can be given a style, as in the window:
any other constraint, a dimension among them, fails with an error
that errors.Is finds ErrNotStylable in, and changes nothing.

String.text:
String describes the constraint as the property browser does, with
its value if it has one: "c002-pt-pt-distance = 40".

Style.text:
Style is the line style the constraint is drawn in: the one it was
given, or else the constraint style.

Type.text: Type is the constraint's type, as the core package names them.

Valid.text:
Valid reports whether the constraint exists: a constraint goes when
what it constrains is deleted.

Value.text:
Value is the constraint's value as the drawing labels it: a length
in mm, an angle in degrees, a ratio.

Doc.text:
Doc is a sketch: the drawing a script reads and changes. Its own
methods find what the drawing holds; what changes it is in the
fields, one for each menu of the window, so that a call is where
the command it does is: doc.Sketch.Line is Sketch > Line Segment,
doc.Features.Extrude is Features > Extrude.

Activate.text: Activate makes g the group that is worked in.

Active.text: Active is the group that is worked in: what is drawn goes into it.

Batch.text:
Batch runs fn in one go. In the application, where each call of
this package waits for the user interface, that is much faster for
a script that makes many things, and the drawing isn't shown half
done.

Constraint.text:
Constraint is the constraint with a description as the property
browser shows it: "c002-pt-pt-distance" or just "c002".

Describe.text:
Describe says what the drawing is, as text, for a reader that can't
see it: the document's unit, the parameters, every group in order
with how it solved, its degrees of freedom, what is wrong with it,
and the volume and bounds of the model up to it, then the active
group's requests and constraints as Group.Describe lists them, and
what is selected. Lengths are in mm. The names it gives are the
ones Doc.Group, Doc.Request and Doc.Constraint take.

Dimension.text: Dimension is the constraint named name.

Entity.text: Entity is the entity with a handle.

Group.text:
Group is the group with a name, or with a description as the
property browser shows it: "g003-extrude" or just "g003". Check
Valid if there may be none.

Groups.text: Groups are the groups, in order, without the references.

Host.text: Host is the program around the sketch.

NewStyle.text:
NewStyle adds a style of the user's own, with the settings a new one
has, as Edit > Line Styles does on the group screen. It is drawn in
nothing until a request or a dimension is given it with
Request.SetStyle or Constraint.SetStyle.

Origin.text: Origin is the point at the origin.

Request.text:
Request is the request with a description as the property browser
shows it: "r004-line-segment" or just "r004".

ResetStyles.text:
ResetStyles puts the program's own styles back to their factory
settings, as Load Factory Defaults does on the styles screen. The
user's own styles are kept. It is one step of undo.

String.text: String describes the document.

Style.text:
Style is the style of that name, as the styles list names it:
"#def-solid-edge" for one of the program's own styles, the name the
user gave a custom one. The call fails when the drawing has none, as
the zero Style it would otherwise give means no style to
Request.SetStyle.

Styles.text:
Styles are the drawing's line styles, in the order the styles list
shows them: the program's own first, then the user's own.

With.text:
With runs fn on the sketch itself, for what this package has no
call for; see the sketch and core packages. The sketch and what is
got from it must not be kept after fn returns. The active group is
taken to have changed.

Workplane.text:
Workplane is one of the three reference workplanes: "XY", "YZ" or
"ZX".

Drawing.text:
Drawing is the model's sheet of views (roadmap step 18): its size,
scale, projection, views and title block. See sketch.Drawing.

DrawingDimension.text:
DrawingDimension is a dimension on a view of the drawing, see
sketch.DrawingDimension.

DrawingMenu.text:
DrawingMenu holds the calls of View > Drawing Sheet and File > Export
> Drawing: the sheet of views, sections and dimensions. A script
reaches it as doc.Drawing.

AddDimension.decl: func (m DrawingMenu) AddDimension(view, kind string, offset float64, edges ...SolidEdge)
AddDimension.text:
AddDimension adds a dimension to the drawing's view: "length"
of an edge, "distance" between two, "diameter" or "radius" of a
circular one; offset is how far its line stands off what it measures,
in sheet mm, out from the view's middle (0 for 10; negative, in toward
it). The dimension holds
the edges' names, so it measures them again as the model changes.
The view is front, back, top, bottom, left, right or iso, where a
length is the edge's in the model, not as foreshortened, or a section
or a detail by its letter (A, B, ...: the sections first).

AddEdgeFaceDistance.decl: func (m DrawingMenu) AddEdgeFaceDistance(view string, offset float64, edge SolidEdge, face SolidFace)
AddEdgeFaceDistance.text:
AddEdgeFaceDistance adds to the drawing's view the distance
from a straight edge to a flat face it runs parallel to, as
AddDrawingDimension does between edges.

AddFaceDimension.decl: func (m DrawingMenu) AddFaceDimension(view, kind string, offset float64, faces ...SolidFace)
AddFaceDimension.text:
AddFaceDimension adds a dimension of faces to the drawing's
view, as AddDrawingDimension does of edges: "distance" between two
parallel flat faces, "diameter" or "radius" of a face's circular
edge, the largest, as a cylinder's or a round end's. The dimension
holds the faces' identities, so it measures them again as the model
changes.

Dimensions.text:
Dimensions measures the drawing's dimensions on the solid as
it is: each one's value in mm, and an error for one that can't be
measured, as for an edge no longer in the solid. It needs the
application, or a view of it.

Export.text:
Export writes the model's drawing to a vector file, by its
extension: .pdf, .svg, .dxf, .eps, .ps, .plt. It needs the
application, or telesapr-cli export-drawing.

Get.text:
Get is the model's drawing, or the default one, an A3 sheet
fitted, if it has none yet. It is a copy: SetDrawing changes it.

Set.text:
Set gives the model the drawing dr: a sheet A4 to A0, Letter
or Tabloid; a scale, 0 to fit; views, none for the standard ones
placed by the projection.

Show.text:
Show shows the drawing sheet in the window in place of
the model, as View > Show Drawing Sheet does, or the model again; it
is view state, not saved. It is an error for a bare sketch with no
application around it (New), or when the sheet can't be made, as when
the active group has no solid. With the sheet shown, Render with the view
"window" pictures the sheet.

Shown.text: Shown reports whether the window shows the drawing sheet.

DrawingView.text: DrawingView is a view on the sheet, see sketch.DrawingView.

EditMenu.text:
EditMenu holds the calls of the Edit menu: undo, regeneration, the
clipboard, the selection, commands and preferences. A script reaches
it as doc.Edit.

CheckClosedContour.text:
CheckClosedContour is whether the closed loops of a sketch are
checked for crossing themselves.

ChordTolerance.text:
ChordTolerance is how closely meshes follow curves, as a percentage
of the model's size.

Copy.text:
Copy puts the entities on the clipboard, with the constraints between
them, as Edit > Copy does with them selected. Workplanes are left out.

MaxSegments.text:
MaxSegments is the most straight pieces a curve is cut into when
meshes are made.

Paste.decl: func (m EditMenu) Paste(move Vec, angle, scale float64) (pasted []Entity)
Paste.text:
Paste adds what is on the clipboard to the active group, in the
active workplane, turned by angle degrees about the workplane's
origin, scaled by scale and then moved by move, as Edit > Paste
Transformed does once; a scale of -1 mirrors it. It returns what
was drawn by pasting, a line for a line, without their points.

Redo.text: Redo does again what Undo took back.

Regen.text: Regen regenerates the whole sketch and solves it.

RunCommand.text:
RunCommand runs a command of the main menu, as choosing it does:
"View > Zoom To Fit", or the entry's own name, "Zoom To Fit", when
only one entry has it. telesapr-cli runs scripts on the interface
without a window, so commands run there too; a document of a Go
program's own, from New, has no menu to run them from, and it is an
error. What the command says went wrong is the error too: a command
that would replace a drawing with unsaved changes, as File > New,
refuses; see ForgetChanges. What the command changes is part of the
script's step of undo.

Select.text: Select selects entities on the drawing, and nothing else.

SelectEdges.text:
SelectEdges selects edges of the solid on the drawing, and nothing
else, as picking them on the model does: for a fillet or a chamfer
made from the menu. The edges must be of the solid at the active
group, which such a group is made after.

SelectFaceEdges.text:
SelectFaceEdges selects the edges that bound the faces, where they
meet other faces, and nothing else, as the context menu's Select Face
Edges does for the faces selected: for a fillet or a chamfer made from
the menu. The faces must be of the solid at the active group.

SelectFaces.text:
SelectFaces selects faces of the solid on the drawing, and nothing
else, as picking them on the model does: for a shell made from the
menu, or a face to draw on. A face an entity made is selected by its
entity, one that no entity names by its identity.

SelectedConstraints.text: SelectedConstraints are the constraints selected on the drawing.

SelectedEdges.text:
SelectedEdges are the edges of the solid selected on the drawing,
picked on the model or by SelectEdges, as edges of the solid at the
active group.

SelectedFaces.text:
SelectedFaces are the faces of the solid selected on the drawing,
picked on the model or by SelectFaces, as faces of the solid at the
active group: a face entity's, or a face no entity names by its
identity. A face is given as the first with its identity.

Selection.text:
Selection is what is selected on the drawing, but for the
constraints.

SetCheckClosedContour.text:
SetCheckClosedContour sets whether the closed loops of a sketch are
checked for crossing themselves (on unless set; the check is slow),
and regenerates everything. A loop that crosses itself is a problem
on the group that uses it only while this is on; a loop that is not
closed always is. In the application it is the setting "check
closed contour" of Configuration, kept with the application and not
in the file.

SetChordTolerance.text:
SetChordTolerance sets how closely meshes follow curves, as a
percentage of the model's size (0.1 unless set; smaller is finer and
slower), and regenerates everything. In the application it is the
setting Configuration shows; scripts that check volumes against a
formula use a fine one.

SetMaxSegments.text:
SetMaxSegments sets the most straight pieces a curve is cut into
when meshes are made, from 7 to 1000 (20 unless set), and
regenerates everything. In the application it is the setting
"max piecewise linear segments" of Configuration. The pieces
exported files cut curves into are ExportOptions.MaxSegments.

Undo.text:
Undo takes back the last step: in a console, what the last line
that changed the sketch did.

Entity.text:
Entity is something on the drawing: a point, a line segment, a
circle, an arc, a curve, a workplane, a normal, a face. What is
drawn makes several: a line segment is an entity and so are its two
ends.

AddSplinePoint.text:
AddSplinePoint adds a point at p to the cubic spline the entity is,
in the span of the spline's points that passes nearest p, as the
context menu's Add Spline Point does where the curve is clicked. The
spline then passes through p, or for a periodic one through it too.

Center.text:
Center is the centre of a circle or an arc, or the origin of a
workplane.

Construction.text:
Construction reports whether the entity is construction geometry,
which helps to draw but makes no part of the outline.

Delete.text:
Delete deletes what was drawn to make the entity, and the
constraints on it.

DeleteCoincidences.text:
DeleteCoincidences deletes the constraints that make the point
coincident with others, as the context menu's Delete Point-Coincident
Constraint does, so it can be dragged away from them.

Dir.text:
Dir is the direction of a line segment, from its start to its end,
or of a normal; it isn't a unit vector for a line.

End.text: End is the other end of a line segment, an arc or a cubic.

FaceNormal.text: FaceNormal is a face's normal, a unit vector.

FacePoint.text: FacePoint is a point a face's plane passes through.

Font.text:
Font is the name of the font file a text is set in; Sketch.Fonts
lists the names.

Free.text:
Free is how much of the entity its group's constraints fix, as the
drawing colours it: sketch.FreedomFixed when it is fully constrained,
sketch.FreedomPartly when some of it can still move,
sketch.FreedomFree when nothing holds it, and sketch.FreedomUnknown
when its group did not solve. Parameters from earlier groups, such
as a workplane's, count as fixed.

Group.text: Group is the group the entity is in.

IsCoincident.text:
IsCoincident reports whether a constraint holds the point
coincident with another point, which is what DeleteCoincidences
takes away.

Kerning.text:
Kerning reports whether a text is set with the font's kerning, the
spacing the font gives to particular pairs of letters.

Kind.text:
Kind names what the entity is: "point", "line", "circle", "arc",
"cubic", "workplane", "normal", "face", ...

Length.text: Length is the length of a line segment, an arc or a circle.

MakePeriodic.text:
MakePeriodic closes the open cubic spline into a periodic one, whose
ends meet: the window does it when a click lands on the first point
again while a point is being placed. A spline that is already
periodic is left as it is. Constraints on the last point move to the
first, those on the points between follow them to their new places,
and those on the control points beside the ends are deleted, as is
one left holding the first point against itself.

MoveBy.text:
MoveBy moves the entity by d: a point, or the points of a line, an
arc, a circle, a cubic, a text or an image, as the arrow keys nudge
the selection; the solver then moves them as the constraints require,
holding them as near where they were put as it can.

MoveTo.text:
MoveTo puts a point at p, as dragging it there does: the solver
then moves it as the constraints require.

Normal.text: Normal is the normal of a circle, an arc or a workplane.

Orientation.text:
Orientation is where the entity's own x and y directions point: for a
normal, and for the workplane, circle or arc that has one, the unit
vectors u and v of its turn (its normal points along u cross v).

Overlap.text:
Overlap is what lies where the point e is, in the groups up to the
active one: the other points at the same position, and the lines,
circles, arcs and cubics that pass through it without a point of
their own there. A click on the drawing picks one of them; the
property browser lists the rest under ALSO HERE, and Edit.Select
selects one from a script.

Points.text:
Points are the points of the entity: the ends of a line, the centre
and the ends of an arc, the centre of a circle, the control points
of a cubic, the origin of a workplane. A point has itself.

Pos.text: Pos is where a point is.

Radius.text: Radius is the radius of a circle or an arc.

RemoveSplinePoint.text:
RemoveSplinePoint takes the point out of the cubic spline it belongs
to, as the context menu's Remove Spline Point does. The points it was
coincident with stay coincident with each other; its other
constraints are deleted. An open spline's ends and their control
points can't be removed.

Request.text:
Request is what was drawn to make the entity; it isn't Valid for an
entity a group made, such as the copies an extrusion makes.

SetConstruction.text: SetConstruction makes what was drawn construction geometry, or not.

SetFont.text:
SetFont sets a text in another font, given by the name of its font
file as Sketch.Fonts lists them; "" is the font built in. It fails for
a font the program doesn't have.

SetKerning.text:
SetKerning turns the kerning of a text on or off, as the text
window's "apply kerning" does.

SetOrientation.text:
SetOrientation turns a normal, or the workplane, circle or arc that
has one, so that its x and y directions point along u and w, which
must not be parallel (w is made square to u), as dragging the normal
in the window does; the solver then moves it as the constraints
require. Only a normal free in 3D can turn: one in a workplane, or
copied from another group, is fixed and the call fails.

SetRadius.text:
SetRadius gives a circle a radius, as dragging it does; constrain
it with Diameter or Radius to keep it.

SetText.text:
SetText changes the string of a text. The text keeps its corner,
direction and height, and the constraints on them, and takes the
width the new string has; the text window's [change] does the same.

Start.text: Start is the first end of a line segment, an arc or a cubic.

String.text: String describes the entity, as "line r004-line-segment".

Text.text: Text is the string of a text drawn with Sketch.Text.

Type.text: Type is the entity's type, as the core package names them.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether the entity exists.

Visible.text:
Visible reports whether the entity is drawn, as the window draws it:
the show flags of View > Show and the group's own show and suppress
modes decide, as PointOfRayCasting and a drawing in the window see
it.

ExportCanvas.text:
ExportCanvas is a 2d file's page when its size is fixed, in mm, and
where the geometry starts on it.

ExportMargin.text:
ExportMargin is the space left around the exported geometry when the
page size is automatic, in mm.

ExportOptions.text:
ExportOptions are the settings that change what an export writes:
the ones the configuration screen shows. Lengths are in mm. Get them
with File.ExportOptions, change the fields and give them back to
File.SetExportOptions; they stay set for the rest of the session and
apply to every export after, whether the script or the window asks.

Quality.text:
Quality is the preset whose chord tolerance, angular tolerance and
segment limit the options hold, or MeshCustom when they match none.

ExtrudeGroup.text: ExtrudeGroup is the view of an extrusion: its draft.

Draft.text:
Draft is an extrusion's draft in degrees: its sides lean into the
solid by that much from the sketch's plane, out when it is negative.

DraftFaces.text:
DraftFaces are the curves of an extrusion's sketch whose sides its
draft leans, or none when it leans every side.

DraftNeutral.text:
DraftNeutral is how far along an extrusion, from the sketch's plane,
its draft's neutral plane lies, in mm: where the solid has the
profile's outline.

SetDraft.text:
SetDraft leans an extrusion's sides into the solid by degrees from
the sketch's plane, so that the far end is smaller (larger when
negative), as a moulded part's; 0 takes the draft away. The profile
must be of lines and arcs; an arc may meet a line at a sharp corner,
but arcs meet each other tangent. A draft at which the sides meet is
a problem on the group, and the extrusion is made without it. SetExpr
with sketch.GroupValC gives it an expression. SetDraftFaces leans
only some sides, and SetDraftNeutral leans them from another plane.

SetDraftFaces.text:
SetDraftFaces makes an extrusion's draft lean the sides of curves
only, the rest staying upright; none leans every side again. A curve
is a line, arc or circle of the extruded sketch, or its copy at an end
of the extrusion, or the face of its side.

SetDraftNeutral.text:
SetDraftNeutral leans an extrusion's drafted sides from the plane mm
along it from the sketch's plane, negative towards a two-sided
extrusion's other end: there the solid has the profile's outline, and
it narrows going away from it both ways, as a moulded part does from
its parting line. 0 is the sketch's plane. A plane off the extrusion
is a problem on the group. SetExpr with sketch.GroupPitch gives it an
expression in the document's unit.

SetSkewed.text:
SetSkewed makes an extrusion's sides lean, or stand straight again,
whether it is one-sided or two-sided, which SetTwoSided keeps.

Skewed.text:
Skewed reports whether an extrusion leans with its sketch's normal
rather than standing straight, as the group screen's "skewed" says.

FeaturesMenu.text:
FeaturesMenu holds the calls of the Features menu: the groups that
start a sketch or make a solid. Each adds a group after the active
one and makes it active. A script reaches it as doc.Features.

BrokenReferences.text:
BrokenReferences lists what the last regeneration that deleted
something deleted, as Edit > Broken References shows it. The list
stays until a regeneration deletes something else, an undo or redo,
or ClearBrokenReferences. Undo brings the deleted items back.

Chamfer.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Chamfer(edges []Entity, distance float64, name string) Group
Chamfer.text:
Chamfer cuts edges of the solid so far, at distance mm from each
edge on both faces that meet there, a 45 degree chamfer where they
are square. An edge is a line segment that lies along an edge
between two flat faces and sticks out, as the copies of the sketch
at the ends of an extrusion and the lines along its sides do; or a
circle or arc where a flat face meets a cylinder or a cone about the
circle's axis, as an extruded circle's or a lathed frustum's, which is
cut all round by a cone. The new group
becomes active.

ChamferSolid.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) ChamferSolid(edges []SolidEdge, distance float64, name string) Group
ChamferSolid.text:
ChamferSolid cuts edges of the solid so far, by name, at distance mm
from each edge on both faces: any straight edge between two flat
faces, such as one a Boolean made, or a circular one where a flat
face meets a cylinder or a cone, picked from Solid. The chamfer
keeps the edges' names, so it follows them when the model upstream
changes, and reports when one no longer resolves. The new group
becomes active.

ClearBrokenReferences.text: ClearBrokenReferences empties the list BrokenReferences gives.

Extrude.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Extrude(depth float64, name string) Group
Extrude.text:
Extrude makes a solid of the active group's sketch by extruding it
by depth along the normal of its workplane, or against it for a
negative depth. The depth is where the extrusion starts, as when it
is dragged; constrain a point of it to keep it. The new group
becomes active.

Fillet.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Fillet(edges []Entity, radius float64, name string) Group
Fillet.text:
Fillet rounds edges of the solid so far with radius mm: line segments
along edges between two flat faces, as the copies of the sketch at
the ends of an extrusion and the lines along its sides are. Each edge
must end at corners of three flat faces. An edge that sticks out is
rounded off, and one that goes in, as a pocket's, is filled. Two
rounded edges that meet at a corner are mitred, their cylinders
meeting along an ellipse, the one that turns further going on past it
when the faces don't lie alike about them; three get a sphere. A
circle or arc where a flat face meets a cylinder or a cone about the
circle's axis, as an extruded circle's, a hole's rim, a boss's foot or
a lathed frustum's top, is rounded all round by a torus. An edge
takes with it the edges it meets smoothly, as round a rectangle whose
corners are rounded. An edge may have a radius of its own
(SetEdgeRadius), but edges that meet at a corner need one. The faces
a fillet makes are exact cylinders, spheres and tori, and their edges
have names. The new group becomes active.

FilletSolid.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) FilletSolid(edges []SolidEdge, radius float64, name string) Group
FilletSolid.text:
FilletSolid rounds edges of the solid so far, by name, with radius
mm, as Fillet does: any straight edge between two flat faces, such
as one a Boolean made, or a circular one, picked from Solid. The fillet
keeps the names, so it follows the edges when the model upstream
changes. The new group becomes active.

Helix.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Helix(axis Entity, degrees, length float64, name string) Group
Helix.text:
Helix makes a solid of the active group's sketch by sweeping it
around a line segment by an angle in degrees while moving it along
the segment's direction by length, as a screw thread does: 360 and a
length of the pitch make one turn. A negative angle turns the other
way. The new group becomes active.

HelixAbout.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) HelixAbout(point, vector Entity, degrees, length float64, name string) Group
HelixAbout.text:
HelixAbout is Helix about an axis through a point and parallel to a
vector, a line segment or a normal.

Lathe.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Lathe(axis Entity, name string) Group
Lathe.text:
Lathe makes a solid of the active group's sketch by turning it all
the way around a line segment. The new group becomes active.

LatheAbout.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) LatheAbout(point, vector Entity, name string) Group
LatheAbout.text:
LatheAbout is Lathe about an axis through a point and parallel to a
vector, a line segment or a normal, as the window takes a point and
a line segment or normal.

Loft.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Loft(from, to Group, name string) Group
Loft.text:
Loft joins the closed loops of two sketches in workplanes, from and
to, with ruled faces, curve by curve, and closes the ends with the
sketches' planes: each loop must be one closed loop; a circle counts
as four curves, and a loop with fewer curves than the other has its
longest split until they match. The solid joins the solid so far as
an extrusion's does. The new group becomes active.

LoftThrough.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) LoftThrough(profiles []Group, name string) Group
LoftThrough.text:
LoftThrough joins the closed loops of sketches in workplanes, three
or more, in order, by one smooth surface through them all, and closes
the ends with the first and last sketches' planes. Loops of fewer
curves have their longest split until all match, and each loop after
the first starts at the curve nearest where the one before it does.
The new group becomes active.

Mirror.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Mirror(plane Entity, name string) Group
Mirror.text:
Mirror reflects the active group in plane, a workplane or a planar
face: its entities are copied reflected, and its solid is reflected
and joined with the original, combined with the model before it as
the active group's solid is, so a mirrored hole is cut too. The
copies follow the plane when it moves. The new group becomes
active; SetKeepOriginal(false) leaves the original out of the
solid.

PatternAlongPath.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) PatternAlongPath(path []Entity, copies int, name string) Group
PatternAlongPath.text:
PatternAlongPath repeats the active group's solid along path, line
segments and arcs joined end to end and meeting tangent, as a sweep's
path, copies times in all: the first where the solid is and the last
at the far end of the path, spaced evenly along it, each turned with
it, as Features > Pattern Along Path does. The path starts at its
end nearest the solid. A path that closes, a circle alone or pieces
that come back to their start meeting it tangent, has the copies
shared out evenly round it, starting at its point nearest the
solid. Copies and SetCopies read and change the
count; the sketch's entities are not copied.

Revolve.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Revolve(axis Entity, degrees float64, name string) Group
Revolve.text:
Revolve makes a solid of the active group's sketch by turning it by
an angle in degrees around a line segment. The new group becomes
active.

RevolveAbout.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) RevolveAbout(point, vector Entity, degrees float64, name string) Group
RevolveAbout.text:
RevolveAbout is Revolve about an axis through a point and parallel to
a vector, a line segment or a normal.

Rotate.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Rotate(n int, center, axis Entity, degrees float64, name string) Group
Rotate.text:
Rotate repeats the model so far n times, each turned by an angle in
degrees from the one before, about an axis through a point: the
direction of a line segment or of a normal, or, with no axis
(Entity{}), the normal of the active workplane. The new group
becomes active.

Shell.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Shell(faces []Entity, thick float64, name string) Group
Shell.text:
Shell hollows the solid so far to walls thick mm, open where the faces
are taken away: face entities, as Group.Faces gives an extrusion's.
This version hollows solids of flat faces, and refuses a thickness at
which walls meet. The faces of the cavity have names. The new group
becomes active.

ShellSolid.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) ShellSolid(faces []SolidFace, thick float64, name string) Group
ShellSolid.text:
ShellSolid hollows the solid so far as Shell does, taking away faces
picked from Solid, such as one a Boolean or a loft made.

Sketch3D.text: Sketch3D adds a group to draw in freely in 3d, and makes it active.

SketchAt.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) SketchAt(origin Entity, u, v Vec, name string) Group
SketchAt.text:
SketchAt adds a group to draw in, in a workplane through a point,
with u to its right and v up; the nearest directions square to each
other are taken. The new group becomes active.

SketchIn.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) SketchIn(wp Entity, name string) Group
SketchIn.text:
SketchIn adds a group to draw in, in a workplane like wp: one of
the reference workplanes, a workplane that was drawn, or the
workplane of another group. The new group becomes active, and its
workplane the one drawn in.

SketchOnFace.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) SketchOnFace(face SolidFace, name string) Group
SketchOnFace.text:
SketchOnFace adds a group to draw in, in a workplane lying in a flat
face of the solid so far, as Solid.FaceAt or Solid.Face give it: its
normal out of the solid, its origin on a corner of the face and u
along an edge of it (for a face with no straight edge, as a
cylinder's cap, the origin at the centre of its circle). The
workplane follows the face when an edit upstream moves it; when the
face is gone, it stays where it was and Problem says so. The new
group becomes active, and its workplane the one drawn in.

SketchOnLines.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) SketchOnLines(origin, lineA, lineB Entity, name string) Group
SketchOnLines.text:
SketchOnLines adds a group to draw in, in a workplane through a point
and parallel to two line segments, as the window makes one from a
point and two line segments: u runs along lineA and v along lineB, each from its start to its end,
and the workplane follows the point and the lines when they move.
The lines must not be parallel. The new group becomes active, and
its workplane the one drawn in.

SketchOnNormal.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) SketchOnNormal(origin, normal Entity, name string) Group
SketchOnNormal.text:
SketchOnNormal adds a group to draw in, in a workplane through a
point and square to a normal (an entity's Normal, or a workplane,
whose normal is taken), as the window makes one from a point and a
normal; the workplane follows the normal when it turns. The new
group becomes active, and its workplane the one drawn in.

Sweep.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Sweep(path []Entity, name string) Group
Sweep.text:
Sweep moves the closed loops of the active group, a sketch in a
workplane, along path, line segments, arcs and cubics joined end to
end and meeting tangent, as a pipe follows its bends. The sweep
starts at the end of the path nearest the sketch's plane, with the
sketch where it is drawn, and keeps its attitude to the path, turning
as little as the path lets it. Along lines and arcs its surfaces are
exact; along cubics they are fitted within a tenth of the chord
tolerance (see also SetTwist and SetSweepUp). Two line segments may
meet at a corner, where the sweep is mitred: each piece cut by the
plane that halves the corner. The new group becomes active.

SweepEdges.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) SweepEdges(edges []SolidEdge, path []Entity, name string) Group
SweepEdges.text:
SweepEdges is Sweep along a chain of edges of the solid so far, by
name (Solid, SolidEdge), and the line segments, arcs and cubics of
path with them, one chain: a straight edge is a line, a circular one
an arc, any other a curve as a cubic is. The sweep keeps the edges'
names, so it follows them when the model upstream changes.

Thread.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Thread(circle Entity, o ThreadOptions) (g Group)
Thread.text:
Thread makes a screw thread on a circle or an arc, about its axis
and from its plane, as Features > Screw Thread does: four groups,
a sketch and a lathe that turn the part down (or bore it), and a
ridge sketch and a helix that sweeps it. It returns the helix group,
which becomes active; its Check says whether the solid came out
sound at the chord tolerance of the moment.

Translate.decl: func (m FeaturesMenu) Translate(n int, delta Vec, name string) Group
Translate.text:
Translate repeats the model so far n times, each a step of delta
from the one before. The new group becomes active.

FileMenu.text:
FileMenu holds the calls of the File menu: loading, saving and
exporting the drawing. A script reaches it as doc.File.

Export.text:
Export writes the sketch in the format the file's extension names:
the mesh of the solid (.stl, .obj, ...), the view (.svg, .dxf, .pdf,
...), the surfaces of the solid (.step), or a picture as Render
makes it (.png).

ExportAs.decl: func (m FileMenu) ExportAs(kind ExportKind, path string) (err error)
ExportAs.text:
ExportAs is Export for a format that can hold several things, such
as a wireframe in a .dxf or a .step.

ExportOptions.text:
ExportOptions are the settings that change what an export writes, as
the configuration screen shows them; see ExportOptions. In a script
run without the application only the mesh export (STL, 3MF) reads
them, and then only ChordTol, MaxSegments and Scale.

ExportSection.text:
ExportSection writes the section of the active group's solid by a
plane as a 2d file (.svg, .dxf, .pdf, ...), as File > Export > 2d
Section does. The plane is the section view's (Doc.Group views'
SetSection) when it is on, and otherwise the active workplane; its
normal is the section's, so a flipped section view lays the section
out mirrored. It needs the application's export writers, as the other
2d exports do.

ForgetChanges.text:
ForgetChanges lets the changes made since the sketch was saved go, as
"Don't Save" does when the application asks: File > New, Open and
the others that replace the drawing refuse to run from a script while
it has unsaved changes, so that nothing is lost unasked. The
drawing itself stays as it is until such a command replaces it.

ImportDXF.decl: func (m FileMenu) ImportDXF(path string) (ignored int, err error)
ImportDXF.text:
ImportDXF adds the entities of a DXF file to the active group, as
File > Import does: in the group's workplane, or, when the file has
entities off the XY plane, as construction entities in 3d, leaving the
workplane (undo brings it back). It returns how many entities of
kinds the importer doesn't know were left out. It is one step of undo.

Load.text: Load replaces the sketch by the one in a .tlspr file.

Render.decl: func (m FileMenu) Render(path string, width, height int, view string) (err error)
Render.text:
Render draws the sketch into a PNG file of width by height pixels,
fitted to it and seen from "top", "bottom", "left", "right",
"front", "back" or "isometric"; or "window", as the application's
window shows it, the same middle and as much of it across.

Save.text:
Save regenerates the sketch and writes it to a .tlspr file. A
SolveSpace model (.slvs) is not written.

SetExportOptions.text:
SetExportOptions replaces the export options, as the configuration
screen does one at a time, and fails, changing nothing, when one is
out of range (see ExportOptions). Take the options with
ExportOptions, change the fields wanted and give them back. In the
application the values are the ones saved with its settings when it
closes.

SetMeshQuality.text:
SetMeshQuality sets the chord tolerance, angular tolerance and
segment limit of the export options to those of the preset q
(MeshDraft, MeshStandard or MeshFine) and leaves the other options
as they are. MeshCustom is not a preset, so it fails; set the fields
with SetExportOptions instead.

Unsaved.text: Unsaved reports whether the sketch changed since it was saved.

FilletGroup.text:
FilletGroup is the view of a fillet: its radius, and the radius of
each edge that has its own.

EdgeRadius.text:
EdgeRadius is the radius in mm a fillet gives its edge i, counting
the entities Edges gives and then the edges SolidEdges gives, from 0:
the edge's own, or the fillet's.

Radius.text: Radius is a fillet's radius in mm.

SetEdgeRadius.decl: func (v FilletGroup) SetEdgeRadius(i int, mm float64)
SetEdgeRadius.text:
SetEdgeRadius gives a fillet's edge i, counted as EdgeRadius counts,
a radius of its own in mm, or with 0 the fillet's again. Rounded
edges that meet at a corner must have one radius; one that ends where
no other rounded edge does may have any.

SetEdgeRadiusExpr.decl: func (v FilletGroup) SetEdgeRadiusExpr(i int, expr string) (err error)
SetEdgeRadiusExpr.text:
SetEdgeRadiusExpr gives a fillet's edge i, counted as EdgeRadius
counts, a radius of its own from an expression in the document's
unit, which may name parameters; "" gives it the fillet's radius
again.

SetRadius.text:
SetRadius sets a fillet's radius in mm; SetExpr with
sketch.GroupPitch gives it an expression in the document's unit.

GCodeOptions.text: GCodeOptions is what an exported G-code file cuts with, in mm.

Group.text:
Group is a group of the sketch: a drawing in a workplane or in 3d,
or a step that makes a solid from the group before it, as an
extrusion does.

AllDimsReference.text:
AllDimsReference reports whether every dimension in the group is
measured without holding the sketch.

AllowRedundant.text:
AllowRedundant reports whether the group may solve with redundant
constraints left in it.

Analyze.text: Analyze measures and checks the solid up to and with the group.

Appearance.text:
Appearance is the group's solid's appearance, "" for the default,
plastic.

AsChamfer.text: AsChamfer is the view of a chamfer.

AsExtrude.text: AsExtrude is the view of an extrusion.

AsFillet.text: AsFillet is the view of a fillet.

AsLink.text: AsLink is the view of a linked part.

AsLoft.text: AsLoft is the view of a loft.

AsMirror.text: AsMirror is the view of a mirror.

AsRepeat.text: AsRepeat is the view of a step and repeat or a pattern along a path.

AsShell.text: AsShell is the view of a shell.

AsSweep.text: AsSweep is the view of a sweep along a path.

Color.decl: func (g Group) Color() (red, green, blue int)
Color.text:
Color is the colour of the group's solid, each of red, green and blue
0 to 255.

Combine.text:
Combine is how the group's solid combines with the solid so far:
Union, Difference, Intersection or Assemble. A step and repeat, a
mirror or a pattern takes its source group's mode, so this is the
source's for those.

Conflicts.text:
Conflicts lists the constraints that keep the group from solving,
as its solve-failure screen does, any one of which could be removed
to fix it; none when the group solved.

Delete.text:
Delete deletes the group and what depends on it. If the active
group goes, being this one or one that used it, the last group
before it that is left becomes active, so that new groups come
where the history ends; Doc.Active says which it is.

Describe.text:
Describe lists what the group holds, as text: how it solved, each
request with where it is, in mm, and each constraint with its value
and what it is on. The names it gives are the ones Doc.Request and
Doc.Constraint take.

Dof.text:
Dof is how many degrees of freedom the group's constraints leave,
or -1 where the group is left out of that count, as SetSuppressDof
asks, and where Doc.Describe says the count was not made.

Edges.text:
Edges are the edges a chamfer cuts or a fillet rounds, or the path a
sweep or a pattern follows.

Entities.text:
Entities are the group's entities, the points and normals among
them.

Expr.text:
Expr is the expression one of the group's values comes from, or ""
for a plain number.

Face.text:
Face is the face of the solid so far that a sketch made by
SketchOnFace lies in.

Faces.text:
Faces are the planar faces this group made, which constraints and
the section view can refer to.

ForceToMesh.text:
ForceToMesh reports whether the group's NURBS surfaces are turned
into a triangle mesh.

History.text:
History is what the group depends on, and where it sits in the list
of groups.

Kind.text:
Kind names what the group is: "sketch-in-plane", "sketch-in-3d",
"extrude", "lathe", "revolve", "helix", "rotate", "translate",
"mirror", "chamfer", "sweep", "fillet", "loft", "shell" or "link".

LeftOut.text:
LeftOut says why the group is left out of the model, or "" if it is
in: "suppressed" for a group suppressed whole, or "uses g004-sketch,
which is suppressed" for one that uses such a group. A group left out
has no entities and no solid of its own, and can't be made active.

Opacity.text: Opacity is how opaque the group's solid is, 0 (clear) to 1.

Param.text:
Param is the group's i-th parameter: for an extrusion, 0 to 2 are
the vector to its middle; for a step and repeat translating, the step; for a
revolve or a step and repeat rotating, 3 is the angle in radians; for a linked
part, 0 to 2 are its move in mm and 3 to 6 the quaternion (w, x, y, z) of its turn,
which LinkGroup.Move, Rotate and SetOrientation set with the group regenerated.

Problem.text:
Problem says what the last regeneration found wrong with the
group's input, as an edge a chamfer can't cut, a sweep path with
a corner, or a sketch that crosses itself, is open, is not flat or
has a curve of no length, with the point where; or "" when there is
nothing. A group with a problem adds no solid. A sketch says what is
wrong with its contours only when a solid is made from it, since a
sweep's path may be open and not flat; the group making the solid
says it too. It also says when the Boolean that joins the group's
solid to the solid so far failed: the group's solid is then
unsound, and Check says where. When the solid so far holds parts
assembled side by side, which may stand in each other, it says so:
a Boolean with such a solid is not defined.

RelaxConstraints.text:
RelaxConstraints reports whether the group's solver keeps only the
coincident constraints and lets the rest of the sketch move.

Requests.text: Requests are what was drawn in the group.

SetAllDimsReference.text:
SetAllDimsReference turns every dimension in the group into a
reference dimension, which is measured and shown but does not hold
the sketch, or makes them constrain again.

SetAllowRedundant.text:
SetAllowRedundant lets the group solve with redundant constraints in
it, or asks for the surplus to be reported as conflicts to remove, as
its solve-failure screen does.

SetAppearance.text:
SetAppearance gives the group's solid an appearance: matte, plastic,
glossy or metal, or "" for the default. Its colour stays. A sketch
makes no solid, so it fails.

SetColor.decl: func (g Group) SetColor(red, green, blue int)
SetColor.text:
SetColor colours the group's solid; each of red, green and blue is
0 to 255. Its opacity stays. Only an extrusion, lathe, revolve,
helix, sweep or loft makes faces of its own colour; a link brings its
own, and a step and repeat, mirror, pattern, chamfer, fillet or shell
keeps the colours of the solid it works on, so those fail.

SetCombine.text:
SetCombine says how the group's solid combines with the solid so
far: Union, Difference, Intersection or Assemble. The extrusion keeps
the direction the script gave it, where the window turns it round,
because a script's depth already says which way a cut goes; a mode
that doesn't exist fails. Only an extrusion, lathe, revolve, helix,
link, sweep or loft has a mode of its own: the others take their
source group's or edit the solid so far, and fail, as the group
screen doesn't offer the choice for them.

SetExpr.decl: func (g Group) SetExpr(value sketch.GroupValue, expr string) (err error)
SetExpr.text:
SetExpr gives one of the group's values text, as typing it on the
group screen does: sketch.GroupCopies for a step and repeat or a pattern,
sketch.GroupPitch for a helix's fixed pitch, a length in the
document's unit (View.Units), sketch.GroupScale for a link. A plain
number is stored as its value; any other text is kept and evaluated
again at each regeneration.

SetForceToMesh.text:
SetForceToMesh makes the group approximate its NURBS surfaces with a
triangle mesh, which an import that carries no such surface needs,
or leaves it to keep them. It does nothing where the model is a
triangle mesh already.

SetOpacity.text:
SetOpacity sets how opaque the group's solid is, from 0 (clear) to 1,
as the group screen's opacity does. Its colour stays. It fails for a
value out of range and for a group with no colour of its own, which
SetColor says.

SetRelaxConstraints.text:
SetRelaxConstraints asks the group's solver to keep only the
coincident constraints, and to treat every other constraint and
dimension as a hint the sketch may not follow, or to require all of
them again. A relaxed group solves where it did not, at the cost of
the dimensions no longer holding.

SetSuppress.text:
SetSuppress leaves the group's solid out of the model with
SuppressSolid; the whole group, its sketch, solve and solid, with
SuppressWhole, which also leaves out every group that uses it; and
puts everything back with Unsuppressed. Nothing is deleted. The
references can't be suppressed whole.

SetSuppressDof.text:
SetSuppressDof leaves the group out of the model's count of free
parameters, which a large group makes quicker to regenerate, or puts
it back in, so that Group.Dof and the screen report the group again.

SetTwoSided.text:
SetTwoSided makes an extrusion, step and repeat, revolve or helix go
both ways from its sketch, or one way when two is false, as the text
window's "two-sided" and "one-sided" do. An extrusion keeps its whole
depth: Extrude(10, ...) then SetTwoSided(true) runs from -5 to 5
along the normal, the sketch in the middle. Copies of a step and
repeat are laid on both sides of the original; a revolve turns as far
each way.

SetVisible.text: SetVisible shows or hides the group.

Solid.text: Solid is the solid at this group: the solid of every group up to it.

SolidEdges.text:
SolidEdges are the edges of the solid a chamfer cuts, a fillet rounds
or a sweep follows, by name.

Solved.text: Solved reports whether the solver satisfied the group's constraints.

String.text:
String describes the group as the property browser does:
"g003-extrude".

SuppressDof.text:
SuppressDof reports whether the group is left out of the model's
count of free parameters, which a large group makes quicker to
regenerate.

Suppression.text: Suppression is the group's suppress mode, as SetSuppress set it.

TwoSided.text:
TwoSided reports whether an extrusion, step and repeat, revolve or
helix goes both ways from its sketch, as the text window's
"two-sided" says.

Type.text: Type is the group's type, as the sketch package names them.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether the group exists.

Value.text:
Value is one of the group's values: the number of copies, the pitch
in mm, or the scale.

Visible.text: Visible reports whether the group is shown.

Workplane.text: Workplane is the workplane of a group that is drawn in one.

GroupAnalysis.text:
GroupAnalysis measures and checks the solid up to and with a group,
as the Analyze menu does for the active group: g.Analyze().

Area.text:
Area is the area in mm² of the closed region the group's sketch
draws, holes taken out, as Analyze > Measure Area gives it with
nothing selected.

Bounds.text:
Bounds are the corners of the box around the model up to and with
this group.

CenterOfMass.text:
CenterOfMass is the centre of mass of the model up to and with this
group, of one density throughout, as Analyze > Show Center of Mass
marks it.

Check.text:
Check checks the solid of the model up to and with this group: it
reports naked and self-intersecting edges, whether the Boolean
failed, the face and triangle counts, and the volume, centre of mass
and bounding box, in mm. Report.Sound() says whether the solid is
closed, does not cross itself, and came from a Boolean that worked,
and is false too when the group added no solid for a Problem (as an
extrusion of a sketch that crosses itself), which Report.Problem
holds; Report.Summary() says it in words. Analyze > Check Solid shows the
same report.

Mesh.text:
Mesh is the triangle mesh of the model up to and with this group.
It is the sketch's own, and is replaced when the sketch
regenerates.

Probe.text:
Probe is where the line through from along dir passes through the
solid of the model up to and with this group, by the ray-cast oracle
(GroupAnalysis.RayCheck): the stretches inside it, in the line's parameter,
dir's length to one. It fails as RayCheck does.

RayCheck.text:
RayCheck checks the solid of the model up to and with this group by
the ray-cast oracle, which rebuilds it from the groups' definitions
(profiles, extrusions, axes, a sweep's steps, where step and repeats,
patterns along a path and mirrors put their copies) without the
kernel's surface intersection: its volume, centre of mass and inertia
tensor about it (Measure.Inertia, for a density of one, in mm⁵;
Measure.PrincipalMoments) by three grids of rays, the rays along
which it and the kernel's mesh disagree by more than twice the chord
tolerance, and the mesh's half-edges (each edge used twice, once each
way). It fails for a model with a group the oracle can't build, as a
fillet or a loft: extrusions, drafted or not, lathes, revolves,
helices, sweeps along lines and arcs, and copies of them only.
Analyze > Ray-Cast Check shows the same.

Shell.text:
Shell is the exact surfaces of the model up to and with this group;
like Mesh, it is the sketch's own.

Triangles.text:
Triangles is how many triangles the model has up to and with this
group.

Volume.text: Volume is the volume in mm³ of the model up to and with this group.

GroupHistory.text:
GroupHistory holds what a group depends on and where it sits in the
list of groups, as Features > Move Group does: g.History().

DependsOn.text:
DependsOn lists the groups this group refers to, in history order:
the group it extrudes or copies, the workplane it is drawn in, and the
groups whose entities its sketch and constraints name. The references
are left out.

MoveBefore.text:
MoveBefore moves the group in the history to just before other, as
one undo step. A move that would put a group ahead of a group it
uses is refused with an error naming both, and nothing changes:
an extrusion can't move before its sketch, nor a sketch after its
extrusion. The references stay first.

MoveToEnd.text:
MoveToEnd moves the group to the end of the history, as MoveBefore
does. Only this group moves: the sketches it uses stay where they
are, as they come before it already. MoveToEndWithSources moves them
along.

MoveToEndWithSources.text:
MoveToEndWithSources moves the group to the end of the history
together with its OwnSources, keeping their order, as one undo step:
an extrusion moves with its sketch. It returns the groups moved, in
their new order. A move that would put one of them ahead of a group
it uses, or another group ahead of one of them that it uses, is
refused with an error naming both, and nothing changes.

MoveWithSourcesBefore.text:
MoveWithSourcesBefore moves the group with its OwnSources to just
before other, as MoveToEndWithSources moves them to the end.

OwnSources.text:
OwnSources lists the group with the groups only it needs, in history
order: those it uses, directly or through each other, that no other
group uses, as an extrusion's sketch. These are what
MoveToEndWithSources moves.

UsedBy.text:
UsedBy lists the groups that refer to this group directly, in
history order.

Host.text:
Host owns a sketch on behalf of a Doc: it is the program around the
sketch, with or without windows. All of it but Run must be called
inside Run.

Interference.text:
Interference is two parts of an assembly that overlap, and the
volume they share in mm³. Approximate is set when the volume is
that of the parts' meshes, within the chord tolerance of their
surfaces, the Boolean of their shells having failed, or that of a
part before a cut that failed on it. Failed is set when nothing is
known of the pair: the Boolean of their shells failed and so did that
of their meshes; Volume is then zero.

LinkGroup.text: LinkGroup is the view of a linked part: the file it links and how.

AsSolid.text:
AsSolid reports whether a link group reads its STEP file as a
solid rather than as a reference mesh.

Info.text:
Info describes the file a link group links, a line each, as the
group's screen shows it: for a STEP file its schema and unit, how
many shapes, faces and triangles it gave, and the chord tolerance it
was tessellated to. A sketch or STL file gives none.

Move.text: Move moves the part by t, in mm, and regenerates it.

Offset.text:
Offset is how far the part is moved from where its file puts it, in
mm.

Orientation.text:
Orientation is where the part's own x and y directions point now, as
unit vectors.

Problem.text:
Problem says what of the file a link group links could not be
read, such as the faces of a STEP file on a kind of surface the
reader does not support, or that the file holds no solid it can
read; "" when all of it was.

Rotate.decl: func (v LinkGroup) Rotate(axis Vec, degrees float64)
Rotate.text:
Rotate turns the part by degrees about the axis through its own
origin, on top of the turn it has, and regenerates it. The turn is
counter-clockwise looking against the axis.

Rotate90.text:
Rotate90 is Edit > Rotate Imported 90°: it turns the part a quarter
about the coordinate axis closest to axis, which the window takes to
be the direction of the view. It is one step of undo.

SetAsSolid.text:
SetAsSolid reads a link group's STEP file as a solid, or as a
reference mesh, and reads it again.

SetOrientation.text:
SetOrientation turns the part so that its own x and y directions
point along u and w, which must not be parallel (w is made square to
u), as dragging the part's normal in the window does.

LoftGroup.text:
LoftGroup is the view of a loft: its profiles, guides, turn and
tangency.

Guides.text:
Guides are a loft's guide curves, the line segments, arcs and cubics
that hold it (see SetGuides), or none.

Profiles.text: Profiles are the sketches a loft joins, in order.

SetGuides.text:
SetGuides holds a loft to guide curves: line segments, arcs and
cubics drawn before it, each chain of them that joins end to end one
guide, from a point of the first profile through every profile to
the last. One guide moves the loft's sections across so that it runs
along the guide; two move, turn and scale them, so that the loft
widens and narrows between them. None takes the guides away. A guide
that misses a profile is the group's problem, with how far.

SetTangency.text:
SetTangency makes a loft leave its first profile square to its plane
and reach its last square to its, the surface's slope across there
start and end times the loft's length; 0 leaves an end free, shaped
by the profiles alone. A loft of two profiles with an end set is one
smooth surface, not ruled patches. SetExpr with sketch.GroupPitch and
sketch.GroupValC gives them expressions.

SetTurn.text:
SetTurn turns a loft's second profile by n curves, which joins its
curves to others of the first: a square lofted to a square turned by
one twists by a quarter.

Tangency.text:
Tangency is how square a loft leaves its first profile and reaches
its last, 0 for an end left free (see SetTangency).

Turn.text:
Turn is how many curves a loft turns its second profile by before
joining curve by curve; a smooth loft turns each after the first.

MeshQuality.text:
MeshQuality names a preset of the mesh export settings (ChordTol,
AngleTol and MaxSegments of ExportOptions): MeshDraft, MeshStandard,
MeshFine, or MeshCustom for any settings that match none.

MirrorGroup.text: MirrorGroup is the view of a mirror: its plane and what it copies.

KeepOriginal.text:
KeepOriginal reports whether a mirror's solid has the original as
well as the reflection.

MirrorSolid.text:
MirrorSolid reports whether a mirror reflects the whole solid so far,
up to and with its source group, rather than the source group's own
solid.

Plane.text: Plane is the workplane or face a mirror reflects in.

SetKeepOriginal.text:
SetKeepOriginal has a mirror's solid keep the original beside the
reflection, or not, which leaves the reflection alone.

SetMirrorSolid.text:
SetMirrorSolid has a mirror reflect the whole solid so far, as a body
made of several groups needs, or only its source group's solid. With
the whole solid, the mirror's result is the solid so far: with its
reflection when it keeps the original, or the reflection alone.

MotionFrame.text:
MotionFrame is a step of a motion study: the parameter's value, the
file its frame went to, if any, whether every group solved, and the
volume of the solid up to the active group.

Param.text:
Param is one of the numbers the solver works out: a coordinate of a
point, a radius, the depth of an extrusion.

Set.text:
Set gives the parameter a value for the solver to start from; what
constrains it decides where it ends.

String.text: String shows the parameter's value.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether the parameter exists.

Parameter.text:
Parameter is a named value of the document's parameter table, which
expressions on dimensions and group values can name, as Edit >
Parameters shows it. It is not a Param, which is one of the solver's
unknowns.

ParamsMenu.text:
ParamsMenu holds the calls of Edit > Parameters: the named numbers
that expressions use, and the configurations that give them other
values. A script reaches it as doc.Params.

ActivateConfiguration.text:
ActivateConfiguration writes the configuration's expressions into
the parameter table and makes it active; "" makes none active, and
leaves the table as it is. The model regenerates.

ActiveConfiguration.text: ActiveConfiguration is the active configuration's name, or "".

AddConfiguration.text:
AddConfiguration adds a configuration, a named set of the parameters'
expressions, from the table as it is, and makes it active: while it
is, SetParameter changes it as well as the table.

Configurations.text:
Configurations are the configurations' names, in the order they were
made.

Delete.text:
Delete removes a parameter. One that an expression names
is not removed, and the error says what names it.

DeleteConfiguration.text:
DeleteConfiguration removes a configuration; the table stays as it
is.

Errors.text:
Errors lists the expressions on constraints and group values
that the last regeneration could not evaluate, each with why; the
values they drive keep their last good value.

Get.decl: func (m ParamsMenu) Get(name string) (p Parameter, ok bool)
Get.text:
Get returns the parameter named name, and whether there is
one.

List.text:
List lists the parameter table, in the order the parameters
were made.

Rename.decl: func (m ParamsMenu) Rename(from, to string) (err error)
Rename.text:
Rename renames a parameter, and rewrites every expression
that names it.

RenameConfiguration.decl: func (m ParamsMenu) RenameConfiguration(from, to string) (err error)

Set.decl: func (m ParamsMenu) Set(name, expr string) (err error)
Set.text:
Set gives the parameter name the expression expr, and adds
it to the table if there is none:
SetParameter("wall", "2.5"), then SetParameter("bore", "wall*4").
An expression that names an unknown parameter, makes a cycle or has
no value is refused, and the table is left as it was. What uses the
parameter regenerates.

Users.text:
Users describes what names the parameter: other
parameters, constraints and group values.

RepeatGroup.text:
RepeatGroup is the view of a step and repeat, translating or
rotating, or of a pattern along a path: how many copies it makes.

Copies.text: Copies is how many copies a step and repeat or a pattern makes.

SetCopies.text:
SetCopies is how many copies a step and repeat or a pattern makes. A
rotate keeps the angle the script gave it, where the window re-spaces
the copies over one turn, because a script states its angle itself.

SetSkipFirst.text:
SetSkipFirst has a one-sided step and repeat start with its first
copy and leave the original out of the solid, or start with the
original again. A rotate keeps the angle the script gave it, where
the window re-spaces the copies when their count is typed. A
two-sided repeat always has the original, and fails.

SkipFirst.text:
SkipFirst reports whether a one-sided step and repeat starts with its
first copy, leaving the original out of the solid, as the group
screen's "start with copy #1" says.

Request.text:
Request is something that was drawn: a line segment, a circle, a
datum point. The property browser lists the requests of a group.

Construction.text: Construction reports whether the request is construction geometry.

Delete.text: Delete deletes the request and the constraints on it.

Entity.text:
Entity is the entity the request makes: the line, the circle. Its
points are that entity's Points.

Group.text: Group is the group the request is in.

SetConstruction.text: SetConstruction makes the request construction geometry, or not.

SetStyle.text:
SetStyle draws the request in the given style, as the window's style
list does for what is selected; the zero Style (api.Style{}) takes
the style away, and the request is drawn in the style it has by where
it is. A request of a point, a workplane or a normal can't be given a
style, as in the window: the call fails with an error that errors.Is
finds ErrNotStylable in, and changes nothing.

String.text:
String describes the request as the property browser does:
"r004-line-segment".

Style.text:
Style is the line style the request is drawn in: the one it was
given, or else the one it has by where it is (construction geometry,
the active group, another).

Type.text: Type is the request's type, as the sketch package names them.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether the request exists.

Section.text:
Section is the state of the section view, as its screen shows it,
and the cut of the active group's solid.

ShellGroup.text: ShellGroup is the view of a shell: the thickness of its wall.

SetThickness.text:
SetThickness sets a shell's wall thickness in mm; SetExpr with
sketch.GroupPitch gives it an expression in the document's unit.

Thickness.text: Thickness is a shell's wall thickness in mm.

SketchHost.text:
SketchHost is a Host for a bare sketch, with no user interface: what
Open and New make outside the application.

Activate.text: Activate makes a group the active one.

AddGroup.decl: func (h *SketchHost) AddGroup(g sketch.Group, seed func(sk *sketch.Sketch, hg core.HGroup)) core.HGroup
AddGroup.text:
AddGroup adds g after the active group, activates it, and
regenerates it and what follows it, a group that makes a solid at the
next read; seed is as for Host.AddGroup.

BeginEval.text:
BeginEval starts a step of a script: its first change is remembered
for undo.

Changing.text:
Changing remembers the sketch for undo before the first change of
a script's step.

Commands.text: Commands is empty: a sketch with no window has no menu.

DeleteGroup.text:
DeleteGroup deletes a group, and regenerates. When the active group
goes, with it or as it used it, the last group before it that is
left is made active.

DrawingSheetShown.text: DrawingSheetShown is false: there is no window.

EndEval.text: EndEval ends a step of a script: what it changed is regenerated.

Export.decl: func (h *SketchHost) Export(kind ExportKind, path string) error
Export.text:
Export writes the mesh as STL; the other formats need the
application around the sketch.

ExportDrawing.text:
ExportDrawing fails: drawing needs the application around the
sketch, or telesapr-cli export-drawing.

ExportOptions.text: ExportOptions are the options set, or those of the settings store.

Hovered.text: Hovered is nothing, for the same reason.

Load.text: Load replaces the sketch by the one in a .tlspr file.

MeasureDrawing.text: MeasureDrawing fails for each dimension, for the same reason.

MmPerUnit.text: MmPerUnit is 1: with no interface, lengths are shown in mm.

Redo.text:
Redo does again the last step undone, and reports whether there was
one.

Remembered.text:
Remembered folds the n steps of undo a change remembered itself into
the script's step: the first of them is the step if the step has
none yet.

Render.decl: func (h *SketchHost) Render(path string, _, _ int, _, _ geom.Vector) error
Render.text: Render fails: drawing needs the application around the sketch.

Rollback.text:
Rollback takes back what the script's last step changed, for good:
it can't be done again as what Undo takes back can. It is false if
the step changed nothing.

Run.text: Run runs fn at once: a bare sketch has no goroutine of its own.

RunCommand.text: RunCommand is an error: a sketch with no window has no menu.

Save.text:
Save writes the sketch to a .tlspr file, its links made relative to
it.

Select.text: Select does nothing, for the same reason.

Selection.text: Selection is nothing: there is no interface to select in.

SetChordTolerance.text:
SetChordTolerance sets the sketch's chord tolerance. The linked
solids are read again at it: a solid keeps the tolerance it was
read at.

SetExportOptions.text: SetExportOptions keeps the options; only the mesh export reads them.

ShowDrawingSheet.text: ShowDrawingSheet fails: there is no window to show the sheet in.

Undo.text: Undo takes back the last step, and reports whether there was one.

SketchMenu.text:
SketchMenu holds the calls of the Sketch menu: what is drawn in the
active group, and the workplane it is drawn in. A script reaches it
as doc.Sketch.

ActiveWorkplane.text:
ActiveWorkplane is the workplane that is drawn in; it isn't Valid
when drawing freely in 3d.

Anywhere3D.text: Anywhere3D draws freely in 3d, in no workplane, in the active group.

Arc.decl: func (m SketchMenu) Arc(center, start, end Vec) Entity
Arc.text:
Arc adds an arc of a circle around center, from start
counter-clockwise to end, in the active workplane. The end is put
at the start's distance from the centre.

Circle.decl: func (m SketchMenu) Circle(center Vec, radius float64) Entity
Circle.text:
Circle adds a circle. In a workplane it lies in it; in 3d it is
parallel to the XY plane.

Cubic.decl: func (m SketchMenu) Cubic(p0, p1, p2, p3 Vec) Entity
Cubic.text:
Cubic adds a cubic Bézier curve from p0 to p3, with the control
points p1 and p2.

Fonts.text:
Fonts lists the TrueType fonts a text can be set in, as the names of
their font files: what Text and Entity.SetFont take, and what the
text window lists.

Image.decl: func (m SketchMenu) Image(path string, at Vec, height float64) Entity
Image.text:
Image adds a picture from a file in the active workplane, for
tracing: its bottom left corner at at, height high and as wide as
the picture's proportions make it. It is construction, as the
interface makes it.

InWorkplane.text:
InWorkplane makes wp the workplane that is drawn in, in the active
group.

Line.decl: func (m SketchMenu) Line(a, b Vec) Entity
Line.text:
Line adds a line segment from a to b. In a workplane the points are
put in it.

NewWorkplane.decl: func (m SketchMenu) NewWorkplane(origin, u, v Vec) Entity
NewWorkplane.text:
NewWorkplane adds a workplane through origin, with u to its right
and v up, to a group drawn freely in 3d.

Point.text: Point adds a datum point at p.

Polyline.text:
Polyline adds the line segments through points, each starting
where the last ended, and back to the first if closed.

Rect.text:
Rect adds a rectangle with the corners a and b and sides along the
active workplane's axes: four line segments, joined, two horizontal
and two vertical, returned starting with the bottom one and going
around counter-clockwise. It makes the same requests and constraints
as the interface's rectangle tool dragged from the top left corner.

Split.decl: func (m SketchMenu) Split(a, b Entity, near Vec)
Split.text:
Split cuts two curves where they cross, or a curve at a point on it,
as Sketch > Split Curves at Intersection does. Of several crossings
it takes the one nearest near.

TangentArc.decl: func (m SketchMenu) TangentArc(point Entity, radius float64, trim bool)
TangentArc.text:
TangentArc rounds the corner at a point where two line segments or
arcs of the active workplane meet, with an arc tangent to both, as
Sketch > Tangent Arc at Point does. radius 0 lets the program choose
it. With trim, the two are cut back to the arc; without, they become
construction and trimmed copies are added.

Text.decl: func (m SketchMenu) Text(text, font string, at Vec, height float64) Entity
Text.text:
Text adds text in a TrueType font in the active workplane, its
bottom left corner at at, and height high; it is as wide as the
font makes it. font is the name of a font file the program knows,
as the text window lists them, or "" for the one built in.

UV.decl: func (m SketchMenu) UV(u, v float64) (p Vec)
UV.text: UV is the point at (u, v) in the active workplane.

Solid.text:
Solid is the solid at a group, as its topology sees it: faces, the
edges where two faces meet, and the vertices where edges end. Its
edges have names that outlive a regeneration, so a script can keep
one and use it after changing the model upstream.

Edge.text:
Edge is the edge a name, as SolidEdge.Name writes it, names; it fails
when the name doesn't resolve, saying why. A name may leave out the
count, "edge A B N" for "edge A B N of M"; the edge has it.

EdgeAt.text:
EdgeAt is the edge nearest the point p, which must be within a
hundredth of a millimetre of it.

Edges.text:
Edges are the solid's edges that lie between two faces, in the
order the topology finds them. The seams between the patches of a
face are none of them, and an edge they cut, as a cylinder's rim, is
one.

EdgesAlong.text: EdgesAlong are the straight edges parallel to dir, either way.

EdgesBetween.text:
EdgesBetween are the edges where faces with the identities of a and
b meet, in the order their names number them: both pieces of a face
another cuts in two count.

Euler.text:
Euler is the solid's Euler characteristic, V - E + F less the holes
in faces: 2 for a solid with no hole through it, 0 for one with one.

Face.text:
Face is the face with identity id, as SolidFace.ID gives it: the
face of which a patch has that identity, whichever patch it is, so a
face of several patches can be named by any of theirs (an extruded
circle's side by any quarter's). It fails for an identity no patch
of the solid has (roadmap 14.1).

FaceAt.text: FaceAt is the face p lies on, within a hundredth of a millimetre.

Problems.text:
Problems lists what is wrong with the solid's topology: edges not
shared by two faces, loops that don't close; none for a sound solid.

SolidEdge.text: SolidEdge is an edge of a solid, by name.

Describe.text: Describe names the edge for a person.

Ends.text:
Ends are the edge's two ends' positions, one point for an edge that
closes, as a circle does.

Faces.text: Faces are the two faces the edge lies between.

Length.text: Length is the edge's length in mm.

Name.text:
Name is the edge's name, "edge A B N": the two faces' identities in
hex and its place among the edges between them. Solid.Edge reads it
back.

Pieces.text:
Pieces is how many pieces the seams of the faces it bounds cut the
edge into: four for an extruded circle's rim.

Points.text: Points are points along the edge, from one end to the other.

Smooth.text:
Smooth reports whether the edge is a seam where its two faces go on
into each other without a crease, as the patches of a loft or a
surface's pieces do: there is no corner there for a fillet or a
chamfer to round.

Straight.text: Straight reports whether the edge is a line segment.

SolidFace.text:
SolidFace is a face of a solid: its identity, the sketch entity that
made it or the group whose surface it is, and which of the faces
with that identity it is. A face may be several patches joined
smoothly, as an extruded circle's side is four.

Edges.text: Edges are the edges round the face.

Entity.text:
Entity is the face entity that made the face, which constraints can
use; it fails for a face that no entity names.

ID.text:
ID is the face's identity: the handle of the entity that made it,
or for a face no entity names, a number made of the group that made
it and its place among that group's surfaces.

Name.text: Name names the face: the entity that made it, or the group.

Neighbours.text: Neighbours are the faces that share an edge with this one.

Patches.text:
Patches is how many patches the face is made of: one for a flat
face, four for an extruded circle's side, more for a surface cut
into patches at its knots.

SolidVertex.text: SolidVertex is a vertex of a solid, by position.

Edges.text: Edges are the edges that end at the vertex.

Style.text:
Style is a line style: how a request or a dimension is drawn, and
whether it goes in an exported file. A script reaches the drawing's
styles as doc.Styles, and makes a new one as doc.NewStyle, which is
what Edit > Line Styles does on the group screen.

The styles the program has of its own — the active group's, a solid
edge's, a datum's — may be changed too, but not deleted, and a
custom style may not be renamed away from what the screen gives it
without the window's edit control: Style.SetName does both, and says
so.

Color.decl: func (s Style) Color() (red, green, blue int)
Color.text:
Color is the style's line colour, each of red, green and blue 0 to
255.

Constraints.text:
Constraints are the constraints, dimensions among them, drawn in the
style.

Custom.text:
Custom reports whether the style is one of the user's own, rather
than one of the program's.

Delete.text:
Delete takes the style out of the drawing; whatever was drawn in it
falls back to the style it would have without one. A style of the
program's own can't be deleted: the program has it of its own, and
makes it again at the next regeneration.

Exportable.text:
Exportable reports whether lines in the style go in an exported
file: a style is exported only when it is both visible and
exportable.

FillColor.decl: func (s Style) FillColor() (red, green, blue int)
FillColor.text:
FillColor is the colour of the contours the style fills, which only
a custom style has.

Filled.text:
Filled reports whether the style fills the contours it draws, which
is how a face or a section cap is given a colour.

Name.text: Name is the style's name, as the styles list shows it.

Requests.text: Requests are what is drawn in the style.

SetColor.decl: func (s Style) SetColor(red, green, blue int)

SetExportable.text:
SetExportable puts the style's lines in exported files, or leaves
them out of them.

SetFillColor.decl: func (s Style) SetFillColor(red, green, blue int)
SetFillColor.text: SetFillColor sets the colour of the contours the style fills.

SetFilled.text: SetFilled fills or stops filling the contours the style draws.

SetName.text:
SetName renames the style, as the style screen's rename does. A style
of the program's own keeps its name: the program finds it by the name
it has, in its settings and in a file.

SetStipple.text: SetStipple dashes the style's lines in the given pattern.

SetStippleScale.text: SetStippleScale sets how far apart the dashes are.

SetTextAlign.text:
SetTextAlign aligns the text of a dimension drawn in the style, as
the style screen's L/H/R and B/V/T links do. horizontal is "left",
"center" or "right"; vertical is "bottom", "center" or "top".

SetTextAngle.text: SetTextAngle turns the text of a dimension drawn in the style.

SetTextHeight.text:
SetTextHeight sets the height of the text of a dimension drawn in the
style.

SetTextHeightAs.text:
SetTextHeightAs measures the text height in pixels (UnitsPixels) or
in millimetres (UnitsMM). The height is converted at the view's
scale, so the text keeps the size it is drawn at, as the style
screen's pixels and mm links do.

SetVisible.text:
SetVisible shows or hides the lines in the style, which leaves the
drawing as it is.

SetWidthAs.text: SetWidthAs measures the width in pixels or in the document's unit.

SetZIndex.text:
SetZIndex draws the style above or below the others: a dimension's
style at 4 puts it over the geometry, which is what the program's
own styles do.
