Shuffle.decl: func (r *Rand) Shuffle(n int, swap func(i, j int))
Shuffle.text: Shuffle pseudo-randomizes the order of elements.

Uint32.text: Uint32 returns a pseudo-random 32-bit value as a uint32.

Uint64.text: Uint64 returns a pseudo-random 64-bit value as a uint64.

Source.text: A Source represents a source of uniformly-distributed pseudo-random int64 values in the range [0, 1<<63).

Source64.text: A Source64 is a Source that can also generate uniformly-distributed pseudo-random uint64 values in the range [0, 1<<64) directly.

Zipf.text: A Zipf generates Zipf distributed variates.

Uint64.text: Uint64 returns a value drawn from the Zipf distribution described by the Zipf object.

ExpFloat64.text: ExpFloat64 returns an exponentially distributed float64 in the range (0, +[math.MaxFloat64]] with an exponential distribution whose rate parameter (lambda) is 1 and whose mean is 1/lambda (1) from the default Source.

Float32.text: Float32 returns, as a float32, a pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0.0,1.0) from the default Source.

Float64.text: Float64 returns, as a float64, a pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0.0,1.0) from the default Source.

Int.text: Int returns a non-negative pseudo-random int from the default Source.

Int31.text: Int31 returns a non-negative pseudo-random 31-bit integer as an int32 from the default Source.

Int31n.text: Int31n returns, as an int32, a non-negative pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0,n) from the default Source.

Int63.text: Int63 returns a non-negative pseudo-random 63-bit integer as an int64 from the default Source.

Int63n.text: Int63n returns, as an int64, a non-negative pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0,n) from the default Source.

Intn.text: Intn returns, as an int, a non-negative pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0,n) from the default Source.

New.text: New returns a new Rand that uses random values from src to generate other random values.

NewSource.text: NewSource returns a new pseudo-random Source seeded with the given value.

NewZipf.decl: func NewZipf(r *Rand, s float64, v float64, imax uint64) *Zipf
NewZipf.text: NewZipf returns a Zipf variate generator.

NormFloat64.text: NormFloat64 returns a normally distributed float64 in the range [-math.MaxFloat64, +[math.MaxFloat64]] with standard normal distribution (mean = 0, stddev = 1) from the default Source.

Perm.text: Perm returns, as a slice of n ints, a pseudo-random permutation of the integers in the half-open interval [0,n) from the default Source.

Read.text: Read generates len(p) random bytes from the default Source and writes them into p.

Seed.text: Seed uses the provided seed value to initialize the default Source to a deterministic state.

Shuffle.decl: func Shuffle(n int, swap func(i, j int))
Shuffle.text: Shuffle pseudo-randomizes the order of elements using the default Source.

Uint32.text: Uint32 returns a pseudo-random 32-bit value as a uint32 from the default Source.

Uint64.text: Uint64 returns a pseudo-random 64-bit value as a uint64 from the default Source.

os.name: os
os.text: Package os provides a platform-independent interface to operating system functionality.

DirEntry.text: A DirEntry is an entry read from a directory (using the ReadDir function or a File.ReadDir method).

File.text: File represents an open file descriptor.

Chdir.text: Chdir changes the current working directory to the file, which must be a directory.

Chmod.text: Chmod changes the mode of the file to mode.

Chown.text: Chown changes the numeric uid and gid of the named file.

Close.text: Close closes the File, rendering it unusable for I/O. On files that support File.SetDeadline, any pending I/O operations will be canceled and return immediately with an ErrClosed error.

Fd.text: Fd returns the system file descriptor or handle referencing the open file.

Name.text: Name returns the name of the file as presented to Open.

Read.text: Read reads up to len(b) bytes from the File and stores them in b.

ReadAt.decl: func (f *File) ReadAt(b []byte, off int64) (n int, err error)
ReadAt.text: ReadAt reads len(b) bytes from the File starting at byte offset off.

ReadDir.text: ReadDir reads the contents of the directory associated with the file f and returns a slice of DirEntry values in directory order.

ReadFrom.decl: func (f *File) ReadFrom(r io.Reader) (n int64, err error)

Readdir.text: Readdir reads the contents of the directory associated with file and returns a slice of up to n FileInfo values, as would be returned by Lstat, in directory order.

Readdirnames.text: Readdirnames reads the contents of the directory associated with file and returns a slice of up to n names of files in the directory, in directory order.

Seek.decl: func (f *File) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (ret int64, err error)
Seek.text: Seek sets the offset for the next Read or Write on file to offset, interpreted according to whence: 0 means relative to the origin of the file, 1 means relative to the current offset, and 2 means relative to the end.

SetDeadline.text: SetDeadline sets the read and write deadlines for a File.

SetReadDeadline.text: SetReadDeadline sets the deadline for future Read calls and any currently-blocked Read call.

SetWriteDeadline.text: SetWriteDeadline sets the deadline for any future Write calls and any currently-blocked Write call.

Stat.text: Stat returns the FileInfo structure describing file.

Sync.text: Sync commits the current contents of the file to stable storage.

Truncate.text: Truncate changes the size of the file.

Write.text: Write writes len(b) bytes from b to the File.

WriteAt.decl: func (f *File) WriteAt(b []byte, off int64) (n int, err error)
WriteAt.text: WriteAt writes len(b) bytes to the File starting at byte offset off.

WriteString.decl: func (f *File) WriteString(s string) (n int, err error)
WriteString.text: WriteString is like Write, but writes the contents of string s rather than a slice of bytes.

WriteTo.decl: func (f *File) WriteTo(w io.Writer) (n int64, err error)

FileInfo.text: A FileInfo describes a file and is returned by Stat and Lstat.

FileMode.text: A FileMode represents a file's mode and permission bits.

LinkError.text: LinkError records an error during a link or symlink or rename system call and the paths that caused it.

PathError.text: PathError records an error and the operation and file path that caused it.

ProcAttr.text: ProcAttr holds the attributes that will be applied to a new process started by StartProcess.

Process.text: Process stores the information about a process created by StartProcess.

Kill.text: Kill causes the Process to exit immediately.

Release.text: Release releases any resources associated with the Process p, rendering it unusable in the future.

Signal.text: Signal sends a signal to the Process.

Wait.text: Wait waits for the Process to exit, and then returns a ProcessState describing its status and an error, if any.

WithHandle.text: WithHandle calls a supplied function f with a valid process handle as an argument.

ProcessState.text: ProcessState stores information about a process, as reported by Wait.

ExitCode.text: ExitCode returns the exit code of the exited process, or -1 if the process hasn't exited or was terminated by a signal.

Exited.text: Exited reports whether the program has exited.

Pid.text: Pid returns the process id of the exited process.

Success.text: Success reports whether the program exited successfully, such as with exit status 0 on Unix.

Sys.text: Sys returns system-dependent exit information about the process.

SysUsage.text: SysUsage returns system-dependent resource usage information about the exited process.

SystemTime.text: SystemTime returns the system CPU time of the exited process and its children.

UserTime.text: UserTime returns the user CPU time of the exited process and its children.

Root.text: Root may be used to only access files within a single directory tree.

Chmod.decl: func (r *Root) Chmod(name string, mode FileMode) error
Chmod.text: Chmod changes the mode of the named file in the root to mode.

Chown.decl: func (r *Root) Chown(name string, uid, gid int) error
Chown.text: Chown changes the numeric uid and gid of the named file in the root.

Chtimes.decl: func (r *Root) Chtimes(name string, atime time.Time, mtime time.Time) error
Chtimes.text: Chtimes changes the access and modification times of the named file in the root.

Create.text: Create creates or truncates the named file in the root.

FS.text: FS returns a file system (an fs.FS) for the tree of files in the root.

Lchown.decl: func (r *Root) Lchown(name string, uid, gid int) error
Lchown.text: Lchown changes the numeric uid and gid of the named file in the root.

Link.text: Link creates newname as a hard link to the oldname file.

Lstat.text: Lstat returns a FileInfo describing the named file in the root.

Mkdir.decl: func (r *Root) Mkdir(name string, perm FileMode) error
Mkdir.text: Mkdir creates a new directory in the root with the specified name and permission bits (before umask).

MkdirAll.decl: func (r *Root) MkdirAll(name string, perm FileMode) error
MkdirAll.text: MkdirAll creates a new directory in the root, along with any necessary parents.

Name.text: Name returns the name of the directory presented to OpenRoot.

Open.text: Open opens the named file in the root for reading.

OpenFile.decl: func (r *Root) OpenFile(name string, flag int, perm FileMode) (*File, error)
OpenFile.text: OpenFile opens the named file in the root.

OpenRoot.text: OpenRoot opens the named directory in the root.

ReadFile.text: ReadFile reads the named file in the root and returns its contents.

Readlink.text: Readlink returns the destination of the named symbolic link in the root.

Remove.text: Remove removes the named file or (empty) directory in the root.

RemoveAll.text: RemoveAll removes the named file or directory and any children that it contains.

Stat.text: Stat returns a FileInfo describing the named file in the root.

Symlink.text: Symlink creates newname as a symbolic link to oldname.

WriteFile.decl: func (r *Root) WriteFile(name string, data []byte, perm FileMode) error
WriteFile.text: WriteFile writes data to the named file in the root, creating it if necessary.

Signal.text: A Signal represents an operating system signal.

SyscallError.text: SyscallError records an error from a specific system call.

Timeout.text: Timeout reports whether this error represents a timeout.

Chdir.text: Chdir changes the current working directory to the named directory.

Chmod.decl: func Chmod(name string, mode FileMode) error
Chmod.text: Chmod changes the mode of the named file to mode.

Chown.decl: func Chown(name string, uid, gid int) error
Chown.text: Chown changes the numeric uid and gid of the named file.

Chtimes.decl: func Chtimes(name string, atime time.Time, mtime time.Time) error
Chtimes.text: Chtimes changes the access and modification times of the named file, similar to the Unix utime() or utimes() functions.

CopyFS.decl: func CopyFS(dir string, fsys fs.FS) error
CopyFS.text: CopyFS copies the file system fsys into the directory dir, creating dir if necessary.

Create.text: Create creates or truncates the named file.

CreateTemp.text: CreateTemp creates a new temporary file in the directory dir, opens the file for reading and writing, and returns the resulting file.

DirFS.text: DirFS returns a file system (an fs.FS) for the tree of files rooted at the directory dir.

Environ.text: Environ returns a copy of strings representing the environment, in the form "key=value".

Executable.text: Executable returns the path name for the executable that started the current process.

Exit.text: Exit causes the current program to exit with the given status code.

Expand.decl: func Expand(s string, mapping func(string) string) string
Expand.text: Expand replaces ${var} or $var in the string based on the mapping function.

ExpandEnv.text: ExpandEnv replaces ${var} or $var in the string according to the values of the current environment variables.

FindProcess.text: FindProcess looks for a running process by its pid.

Getegid.text: Getegid returns the numeric effective group id of the caller.

Getenv.text: Getenv retrieves the value of the environment variable named by the key.

Geteuid.text: Geteuid returns the numeric effective user id of the caller.

Getgid.text: Getgid returns the numeric group id of the caller.

Getgroups.text: Getgroups returns a list of the numeric ids of groups that the caller belongs to.

Getpagesize.text: Getpagesize returns the underlying system's memory page size.

Getpid.text: Getpid returns the process id of the caller.

Getppid.text: Getppid returns the process id of the caller's parent.

Getuid.text: Getuid returns the numeric user id of the caller.

Getwd.text: Getwd returns an absolute path name corresponding to the current directory.

Hostname.text: Hostname returns the host name reported by the kernel.

IsExist.text: IsExist returns a boolean indicating whether its argument is known to report that a file or directory already exists.

IsNotExist.text: IsNotExist returns a boolean indicating whether its argument is known to report that a file or directory does not exist.

IsPathSeparator.text: IsPathSeparator reports whether c is a directory separator character.

IsPermission.text: IsPermission returns a boolean indicating whether its argument is known to report that permission is denied.

IsTimeout.text: IsTimeout returns a boolean indicating whether its argument is known to report that a timeout occurred.

Lchown.decl: func Lchown(name string, uid, gid int) error
Lchown.text: Lchown changes the numeric uid and gid of the named file.

Link.text: Link creates newname as a hard link to the oldname file.

LookupEnv.text: LookupEnv retrieves the value of the environment variable named by the key.

Lstat.text: Lstat returns a FileInfo describing the named file.

Mkdir.decl: func Mkdir(name string, perm FileMode) error
Mkdir.text: Mkdir creates a new directory with the specified name and permission bits (before umask).

MkdirAll.decl: func MkdirAll(path string, perm FileMode) error
MkdirAll.text: MkdirAll creates a directory named path, along with any necessary parents, and returns nil, or else returns an error.

MkdirTemp.text: MkdirTemp creates a new temporary directory in the directory dir and returns the pathname of the new directory.

NewFile.text: NewFile returns a new File with the given file descriptor and name.

NewSyscallError.decl: func NewSyscallError(syscall string, err error) error
NewSyscallError.text: NewSyscallError returns, as an error, a new SyscallError with the given system call name and error details.

Open.text: Open opens the named file for reading.

OpenFile.decl: func OpenFile(name string, flag int, perm FileMode) (*File, error)
OpenFile.text: OpenFile is the generalized open call; most users will use Open or Create instead.

OpenInRoot.text: OpenInRoot opens the file name in the directory dir.

Pipe.text: Pipe returns a connected pair of Files; reads from r return bytes written to w.

ReadDir.text: ReadDir reads the named directory, returning all its directory entries sorted by filename.

ReadFile.text: ReadFile reads the named file and returns the contents.

Readlink.text: Readlink returns the destination of the named symbolic link.

Remove.text: Remove removes the named file or (empty) directory.

RemoveAll.text: RemoveAll removes path and any children it contains.

SameFile.text: SameFile reports whether fi1 and fi2 describe the same file.

Setenv.text: Setenv sets the value of the environment variable named by the key.

StartProcess.decl: func StartProcess(name string, argv []string, attr *ProcAttr) (*Process, error)
StartProcess.text: StartProcess starts a new process with the program, arguments and attributes specified by name, argv and attr.

Stat.text: Stat returns a FileInfo describing the named file.

Symlink.text: Symlink creates newname as a symbolic link to oldname.

TempDir.text: TempDir returns the default directory to use for temporary files.

Truncate.decl: func Truncate(name string, size int64) error
Truncate.text: Truncate changes the size of the named file.

Unsetenv.text: Unsetenv unsets a single environment variable.

UserCacheDir.text: UserCacheDir returns the default root directory to use for user-specific cached data.

Dir.text: Dir returns all but the last element of path, typically the path's directory.

Ext.text: Ext returns the file name extension used by path.

Join.text: Join joins any number of path elements into a single path, separating them with an OS specific Separator.

ErrBadPattern.text: ErrBadPattern indicates a pattern was malformed.

regexp.name: regexp
regexp.text: Package regexp implements regular expression search.

Regexp.text: Regexp is the representation of a compiled regular expression.

Copy.text: Copy returns a new Regexp object copied from re.

Expand.text: Expand appends template to dst and returns the result; during the append, Expand replaces variables in the template with corresponding matches drawn from src.

ExpandString.decl: func (re *Regexp) ExpandString(dst []byte, template string, src string, match []int) []byte
ExpandString.text: ExpandString is like Regexp.Expand but the template and source are strings.

Find.text: Find returns the text of the leftmost match for re in b.

FindAll.text: FindAll returns all the matches for re in b.

FindAllIndex.text: FindAllIndex returns the locations of all matches for re in b.

FindAllString.text: FindAllString returns all the matches for re in s.

FindAllStringIndex.text: FindAllStringIndex returns the locations of all matches for re in s.

FindAllStringSubmatchIndex.text: FindAllStringSubmatchIndex returns the locations of all matches for re in s, including submatch locations.

FindAllSubmatchIndex.text: FindAllSubmatchIndex returns the locations of all matches for re in b, including submatch locations.

FindIndex.text: FindIndex returns the location of the leftmost match for re in b.

FindReaderIndex.text: FindReaderIndex returns the location of the leftmost match for re in r.

FindReaderSubmatchIndex.text: FindReaderSubmatchIndex returns the first match for re in r, including submatches.

FindString.text: FindString returns the text of the leftmost match for re in s.

FindStringIndex.text: FindStringIndex returns the location of the leftmost match for re in s.

FindStringSubmatch.text: FindStringSubmatch returns the first match for re in s, including submatches.

FindStringSubmatchIndex.text: FindStringSubmatchIndex returns the first match for re in s, including submatches.

FindSubmatch.text: FindSubmatch returns the first match for re in b, including submatches.

FindSubmatchIndex.text: FindSubmatchIndex returns the first match for re in b, including submatches.

LiteralPrefix.text: LiteralPrefix returns a literal string that must begin any match of the regular expression re.

Longest.text: Longest makes future searches prefer the leftmost-longest match.

Match.text: Match reports whether the byte slice b contains any match of the regular expression re.

MatchReader.text: MatchReader reports whether the text returned by the io.RuneReader contains any match of the regular expression re.

MatchString.text: MatchString reports whether the string s contains any match of the regular expression re.

NumSubexp.text: NumSubexp returns the number of parenthesized subexpressions in this Regexp.

ReplaceAll.text: ReplaceAll returns a copy of src, replacing matches of the Regexp with the replacement text repl.

ReplaceAllFunc.text: ReplaceAllFunc returns a copy of src in which all matches of the Regexp have been replaced by the return value of function repl applied to the matched byte slice.

ReplaceAllLiteral.text: ReplaceAllLiteral returns a copy of src, replacing matches of the Regexp with the replacement bytes repl.

ReplaceAllLiteralString.text: ReplaceAllLiteralString returns a copy of src, replacing matches of the Regexp with the replacement string repl.

ReplaceAllString.text: ReplaceAllString returns a copy of src, replacing matches of the Regexp with the replacement string repl.

ReplaceAllStringFunc.decl: func (re *Regexp) ReplaceAllStringFunc(src string, repl func(string) string) string
ReplaceAllStringFunc.text: ReplaceAllStringFunc returns a copy of src in which all matches of the Regexp have been replaced by the return value of function repl applied to the matched substring.

Split.text: Split slices s into substrings separated by the expression and returns a slice of the substrings between those expression matches.

String.text: String returns the source text used to compile the regular expression.

SubexpIndex.text: SubexpIndex returns the index of the first subexpression with the given name, or -1 if there is no subexpression with that name.

SubexpNames.text: SubexpNames returns the names of the parenthesized subexpressions in this Regexp.

UnmarshalText.text: UnmarshalText implements encoding.TextUnmarshaler by calling Compile on the encoded value.

Compile.text: Compile parses a regular expression and returns, if successful, a Regexp object that can be used to match against text.

Match.decl: func Match(pattern string, b []byte) (matched bool, err error)

MatchString.decl: func MatchString(pattern string, s string) (matched bool, err error)

MustCompilePOSIX.text: MustCompilePOSIX is like CompilePOSIX but panics if the expression cannot be parsed.

sort.name: sort
sort.text: Package sort provides primitives for sorting slices and user-defined collections.

Float64Slice.text: Float64Slice implements Interface for a []float64, sorting in increasing order, with not-a-number (NaN) values ordered before other values.

Less.decl: func (x Float64Slice) Less(i, j int) bool
Less.text: Less reports whether x[i] should be ordered before x[j], as required by the sort Interface.

Search.text: Search returns the result of applying SearchFloat64s to the receiver and x.

IntSlice.text: IntSlice attaches the methods of Interface to []int, sorting in increasing order.

Less.decl: func (x IntSlice) Less(i, j int) bool

Search.text: Search returns the result of applying SearchInts to the receiver and x.

Sort.text: Sort is a convenience method: x.Sort() calls Sort(x).

Interface.text: An implementation of Interface can be sorted by the routines in this package.

StringSlice.text: StringSlice attaches the methods of Interface to []string, sorting in increasing order.

Less.decl: func (x StringSlice) Less(i, j int) bool

Search.text: Search returns the result of applying SearchStrings to the receiver and x.

Sort.text: Sort is a convenience method: x.Sort() calls Sort(x).

Find.decl: func Find(n int, cmp func(int) int) (i int, found bool)
Find.text: Find uses binary search to find and return the smallest index i in [0, n) at which cmp(i) <= 0.

Float64s.text: Float64s sorts a slice of float64s in increasing order.

Float64sAreSorted.text: Float64sAreSorted reports whether the slice x is sorted in increasing order, with not-a-number (NaN) values before any other values.

Ints.text: Ints sorts a slice of ints in increasing order.

IntsAreSorted.text: IntsAreSorted reports whether the slice x is sorted in increasing order.

IsSorted.text: IsSorted reports whether data is sorted.

Reverse.text: Reverse returns the reverse order for data.

Search.decl: func Search(n int, f func(int) bool) int
Search.text: Search uses binary search to find and return the smallest index i in [0, n) at which f(i) is true, assuming that on the range [0, n), f(i) == true implies f(i+1) == true.

SearchFloat64s.text: SearchFloat64s searches for x in a sorted slice of float64s and returns the index as specified by Search.

SearchInts.text: SearchInts searches for x in a sorted slice of ints and returns the index as specified by Search.

SearchStrings.text: SearchStrings searches for x in a sorted slice of strings and returns the index as specified by Search.

Slice.decl: func Slice(x any, less func(i, j int) bool)
Slice.text: Slice sorts the slice x given the provided less function.

SliceIsSorted.decl: func SliceIsSorted(x any, less func(i, j int) bool) bool
SliceIsSorted.text: SliceIsSorted reports whether the slice x is sorted according to the provided less function.

SliceStable.decl: func SliceStable(x any, less func(i, j int) bool)
SliceStable.text: SliceStable sorts the slice x using the provided less function, keeping equal elements in their original order.

Sort.text: Sort sorts data in ascending order as determined by the Less method.

Stable.text: Stable sorts data in ascending order as determined by the Less method, while keeping the original order of equal elements.

Strings.text: Strings sorts a slice of strings in increasing order.

StringsAreSorted.text: StringsAreSorted reports whether the slice x is sorted in increasing order.

AppendInt.text: AppendInt appends the string form of the integer i, as generated by FormatInt, to dst and returns the extended buffer.

AppendQuoteToGraphic.text: AppendQuoteToGraphic appends a double-quoted Go string literal representing s, as generated by QuoteToGraphic, to dst and returns the extended buffer.

CanBackquote.text: CanBackquote reports whether the string s can be represented unchanged as a single-line backquoted string without control characters other than tab.

FormatBool.text: FormatBool returns "true" or "false" according to the value of b.

FormatComplex.decl: func FormatComplex(c complex128, fmt byte, prec, bitSize int) string
FormatComplex.text: FormatComplex converts the complex number c to a string of the form (a+bi) where a and b are the real and imaginary parts, formatted according to the format fmt and precision prec.

FormatFloat.decl: func FormatFloat(f float64, fmt byte, prec, bitSize int) string
FormatFloat.text: FormatFloat converts the floating-point number f to a string, according to the format fmt and precision prec.

FormatInt.decl: func FormatInt(i int64, base int) string
FormatInt.text: FormatInt returns the string representation of i in the given base, for 2 <= base <= 36.

FormatUint.decl: func FormatUint(i uint64, base int) string
FormatUint.text: FormatUint returns the string representation of i in the given base, for 2 <= base <= 36.

IsGraphic.text: IsGraphic reports whether the rune is defined as a Graphic by Unicode.

ParseBool.text: ParseBool returns the boolean value represented by the string.

ParseComplex.decl: func ParseComplex(s string, bitSize int) (complex128, error)
ParseComplex.text: ParseComplex converts the string s to a complex number with the precision specified by bitSize: 64 for complex64, or 128 for complex128.

ParseFloat.decl: func ParseFloat(s string, bitSize int) (float64, error)
ParseFloat.text: ParseFloat converts the string s to a floating-point number with the precision specified by bitSize: 32 for float32, or 64 for float64.

ParseInt.decl: func ParseInt(s string, base int, bitSize int) (i int64, err error)
ParseInt.text: ParseInt interprets a string s in the given base (0, 2 to 36) and bit size (0 to 64) and returns the corresponding value i.

ParseUint.decl: func ParseUint(s string, base int, bitSize int) (uint64, error)
ParseUint.text: ParseUint is like ParseInt but for unsigned numbers.

QuoteRuneToGraphic.text: QuoteRuneToGraphic returns a single-quoted Go character literal representing the rune.

QuoteToGraphic.text: QuoteToGraphic returns a double-quoted Go string literal representing s.

QuotedPrefix.text: QuotedPrefix returns the quoted string (as understood by Unquote) at the prefix of s.

UnquoteChar.decl: func UnquoteChar(s string, quote byte) (value rune, multibyte bool, tail string, err error)
UnquoteChar.text: UnquoteChar decodes the first character or byte in the escaped string or character literal represented by the string s.

ErrRange.text: ErrRange indicates that a value is out of range for the target type.

ErrSyntax.text: ErrSyntax indicates that a value does not have the right syntax for the target type.

IntSize.text: IntSize is the size in bits of an int or uint value.

strings.name: strings
strings.text: Package strings implements simple functions to manipulate UTF-8 encoded strings.

Builder.text: A Builder is used to efficiently build a string using Builder.Write methods.

Cap.text: Cap returns the capacity of the builder's underlying byte slice.

Grow.text: Grow grows b's capacity, if necessary, to guarantee space for another n bytes.

Len.text: Len returns the number of accumulated bytes; b.Len() == len(b.String()).

Reset.text: Reset resets the Builder to be empty.

String.text: String returns the accumulated string.

Write.text: Write appends the contents of p to b's buffer.

WriteByte.text: WriteByte appends the byte c to b's buffer.

WriteRune.text: WriteRune appends the UTF-8 encoding of Unicode code point r to b's buffer.

WriteString.text: WriteString appends the contents of s to b's buffer.

Reader.text: A Reader implements the io.Reader, io.ReaderAt, io.ByteReader, io.ByteScanner, io.RuneReader, io.RuneScanner, io.Seeker, and io.WriterTo interfaces by reading from a string.

Len.text: Len returns the number of bytes of the unread portion of the string.

ReadAt.decl: func (r *Reader) ReadAt(b []byte, off int64) (n int, err error)

ReadRune.decl: func (r *Reader) ReadRune() (ch rune, size int, err error)

Reset.text: Reset resets the Reader to be reading from s.

Seek.decl: func (r *Reader) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error)

Size.text: Size returns the original length of the underlying string.

WriteTo.decl: func (r *Reader) WriteTo(w io.Writer) (n int64, err error)

Replace.text: Replace returns a copy of s with all replacements performed.

WriteString.decl: func (r *Replacer) WriteString(w io.Writer, s string) (n int, err error)
WriteString.text: WriteString writes s to w with all replacements performed.

Compare.text: Compare returns an integer comparing two strings lexicographically.

Contains.text: Contains reports whether substr is within s.

ContainsAny.text: ContainsAny reports whether any Unicode code points in chars are within s.

ContainsFunc.decl: func ContainsFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) bool
ContainsFunc.text: ContainsFunc reports whether any Unicode code points r within s satisfy f(r).

ContainsRune.decl: func ContainsRune(s string, r rune) bool
ContainsRune.text: ContainsRune reports whether the Unicode code point r is within s.

Count.text: Count counts the number of non-overlapping instances of substr in s.

Cut.decl: func Cut(s, sep string) (before, after string, found bool)
Cut.text: Cut slices s around the first instance of sep, returning the text before and after sep.

CutLast.decl: func CutLast(s, sep string) (before, after string, found bool)
CutLast.text: CutLast slices s around the last instance of sep, returning the text before and after sep.

CutPrefix.decl: func CutPrefix(s, prefix string) (after string, found bool)
CutPrefix.text: CutPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix string and reports whether it found the prefix.

CutSuffix.decl: func CutSuffix(s, suffix string) (before string, found bool)
CutSuffix.text: CutSuffix returns s without the provided ending suffix string and reports whether it found the suffix.

EqualFold.text: EqualFold reports whether s and t, interpreted as UTF-8 strings, are equal under simple Unicode case-folding, which is a more general form of case-insensitivity.

Fields.text: Fields splits the string s around each instance of one or more consecutive white space characters, as defined by unicode.IsSpace, returning a slice of substrings of s or an empty slice if s contains only white space.

FieldsFunc.decl: func FieldsFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) []string
FieldsFunc.text: FieldsFunc splits the string s at each run of Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) and returns an array of slices of s.

FieldsFuncSeq.decl: func FieldsFuncSeq(s string, f func(rune) bool) iter.Seq[string]
FieldsFuncSeq.text: FieldsFuncSeq returns an iterator over substrings of s split around runs of Unicode code points satisfying f(c).

FieldsSeq.text: FieldsSeq returns an iterator over substrings of s split around runs of whitespace characters, as defined by unicode.IsSpace.

HasPrefix.text: HasPrefix reports whether the string s begins with prefix.

HasSuffix.text: HasSuffix reports whether the string s ends with suffix.

Index.text: Index returns the index of the first instance of substr in s, or -1 if substr is not present in s.

IndexAny.text: IndexAny returns the index of the first instance of any Unicode code point from chars in s, or -1 if no Unicode code point from chars is present in s.

IndexByte.decl: func IndexByte(s string, c byte) int
IndexByte.text: IndexByte returns the index of the first instance of c in s, or -1 if c is not present in s.

IndexFunc.decl: func IndexFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) int
IndexFunc.text: IndexFunc returns the index into s of the first Unicode code point satisfying f(c), or -1 if none do.

IndexRune.decl: func IndexRune(s string, r rune) int
IndexRune.text: IndexRune returns the index of the first instance of the Unicode code point r, or -1 if rune is not present in s.

Join.text: Join concatenates the elements of its first argument to create a single string.

LastIndex.text: LastIndex returns the index of the last instance of substr in s, or -1 if substr is not present in s.

LastIndexAny.text: LastIndexAny returns the index of the last instance of any Unicode code point from chars in s, or -1 if no Unicode code point from chars is present in s.

LastIndexByte.decl: func LastIndexByte(s string, c byte) int
LastIndexByte.text: LastIndexByte returns the index of the last instance of c in s, or -1 if c is not present in s.

LastIndexFunc.decl: func LastIndexFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) int
LastIndexFunc.text: LastIndexFunc returns the index into s of the last Unicode code point satisfying f(c), or -1 if none do.

Lines.text: Lines returns an iterator over the newline-terminated lines in the string s.

Map.decl: func Map(mapping func(rune) rune, s string) string
Map.text: Map returns a copy of the string s with all its characters modified according to the mapping function.

NewReader.text: NewReader returns a new Reader reading from s.

NewReplacer.text: NewReplacer returns a new Replacer from a list of old, new string pairs.

Repeat.decl: func Repeat(s string, count int) string
Repeat.text: Repeat returns a new string consisting of count copies of the string s.

Replace.decl: func Replace(s, old, new string, n int) string
Replace.text: Replace returns a copy of the string s with the first n non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new.

ReplaceAll.decl: func ReplaceAll(s, old, new string) string
ReplaceAll.text: ReplaceAll returns a copy of the string s with all non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new.

Split.text: Split slices s into all substrings separated by sep and returns a slice of the substrings between those separators.

SplitAfter.text: SplitAfter slices s into all substrings after each instance of sep and returns a slice of those substrings.

SplitAfterN.decl: func SplitAfterN(s, sep string, n int) []string
SplitAfterN.text: SplitAfterN slices s into substrings after each instance of sep and returns a slice of those substrings.

SplitAfterSeq.text: SplitAfterSeq returns an iterator over substrings of s split after each instance of sep.

SplitN.decl: func SplitN(s, sep string, n int) []string
SplitN.text: SplitN slices s into substrings separated by sep and returns a slice of the substrings between those separators.

SplitSeq.text: SplitSeq returns an iterator over all substrings of s separated by sep.

Title.text: Title returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters that begin words mapped to their Unicode title case.

ToLower.text: ToLower returns s with all Unicode letters mapped to their lower case.

ToLowerSpecial.decl: func ToLowerSpecial(c unicode.SpecialCase, s string) string
ToLowerSpecial.text: ToLowerSpecial returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their lower case using the case mapping specified by c.

ToTitle.text: ToTitle returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their Unicode title case.

ToTitleSpecial.decl: func ToTitleSpecial(c unicode.SpecialCase, s string) string
ToTitleSpecial.text: ToTitleSpecial returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their Unicode title case, giving priority to the special casing rules.

ToUpper.text: ToUpper returns s with all Unicode letters mapped to their upper case.

ToUpperSpecial.decl: func ToUpperSpecial(c unicode.SpecialCase, s string) string
ToUpperSpecial.text: ToUpperSpecial returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their upper case using the case mapping specified by c.

ToValidUTF8.text: ToValidUTF8 returns a copy of the string s with each run of invalid UTF-8 byte sequences replaced by the replacement string, which may be empty.

Trim.text: Trim returns a slice of the string s with all leading and trailing Unicode code points contained in cutset removed.

TrimFunc.decl: func TrimFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) string
TrimFunc.text: TrimFunc returns a slice of the string s with all leading and trailing Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) removed.

TrimLeft.text: TrimLeft returns a slice of the string s with all leading Unicode code points contained in cutset removed.

TrimLeftFunc.decl: func TrimLeftFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) string
TrimLeftFunc.text: TrimLeftFunc returns a slice of the string s with all leading Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) removed.

TrimPrefix.text: TrimPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix string.

TrimRight.text: TrimRight returns a slice of the string s, with all trailing Unicode code points contained in cutset removed.

TrimRightFunc.decl: func TrimRightFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) string
TrimRightFunc.text: TrimRightFunc returns a slice of the string s with all trailing Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) removed.

TrimSpace.text: TrimSpace returns a slice (substring) of the string s, with all leading and trailing white space removed, as defined by Unicode.

TrimSuffix.text: TrimSuffix returns s without the provided trailing suffix string.

sync.name: sync
sync.text: Package sync provides basic synchronization primitives such as mutual exclusion locks.

Cond.text: Cond implements a condition variable, a rendezvous point for goroutines waiting for or announcing the occurrence of an event.

Broadcast.text: Broadcast wakes all goroutines waiting on c.

Signal.text: Signal wakes one goroutine waiting on c, if there is any.

Wait.text: Wait atomically unlocks c.L and suspends execution of the calling goroutine.

Locker.text: A Locker represents an object that can be locked and unlocked.

Map.text: Map is like a Go map[any]any but is safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines without additional locking or coordination.

Clear.text: Clear deletes all the entries, resulting in an empty Map.

CompareAndDelete.text: CompareAndDelete deletes the entry for key if its value is equal to old.

CompareAndSwap.decl: func (m *Map) CompareAndSwap(key, old, new any) (swapped bool)
CompareAndSwap.text: CompareAndSwap swaps the old and new values for key if the value stored in the map is equal to old.

Delete.text: Delete deletes the value for a key.

Load.decl: func (m *Map) Load(key any) (value any, ok bool)
Load.text: Load returns the value stored in the map for a key, or nil if no value is present.

LoadAndDelete.decl: func (m *Map) LoadAndDelete(key any) (value any, loaded bool)
LoadAndDelete.text: LoadAndDelete deletes the value for a key, returning the previous value if any.

LoadOrStore.decl: func (m *Map) LoadOrStore(key, value any) (actual any, loaded bool)
LoadOrStore.text: LoadOrStore returns the existing value for the key if present.

Range.decl: func (m *Map) Range(f func(key, value any) bool)
Range.text: Range calls f sequentially for each key and value present in the map.

Store.text: Store sets the value for a key.

Swap.decl: func (m *Map) Swap(key, value any) (previous any, loaded bool)
Swap.text: Swap swaps the value for a key and returns the previous value if any.

Mutex.text: A Mutex is a mutual exclusion lock.

TryLock.text: TryLock tries to lock m and reports whether it succeeded.

Once.text: Once is an object that will perform exactly one action.

Do.text: Do calls the function f if and only if Do is being called for the first time for this instance of Once.

Pool.text: A Pool is a set of temporary objects that may be individually saved and retrieved.

Get.text: Get selects an arbitrary item from the Pool, removes it from the Pool, and returns it to the caller.

Put.text: Put adds x to the pool.

RWMutex.text: A RWMutex is a reader/writer mutual exclusion lock.

RLocker.text: RLocker returns a Locker interface that implements the Locker.Lock and Locker.Unlock methods by calling rw.RLock and rw.RUnlock.

RUnlock.text: RUnlock undoes a single RWMutex.RLock call; it does not affect other simultaneous readers.

TryLock.text: TryLock tries to lock rw for writing and reports whether it succeeded.

TryRLock.text: TryRLock tries to lock rw for reading and reports whether it succeeded.

WaitGroup.text: A WaitGroup is a counting semaphore typically used to wait for a group of goroutines or tasks to finish.

Add.text: Add adds delta, which may be negative, to the WaitGroup task counter.

Done.text: Done decrements the WaitGroup task counter by one.

Go.text: Go calls f in a new goroutine and adds that task to the WaitGroup.

Wait.text: Wait blocks until the WaitGroup task counter is zero.

NewCond.text: NewCond returns a new Cond with Locker l.

OnceFunc.text: OnceFunc returns a function that invokes f only once.

OnceValue.decl: func OnceValue[T any](f func() T) func() T
OnceValue.text: OnceValue returns a function that invokes f only once and returns the value returned by f.

OnceValues.decl: func OnceValues[T1, T2 any](f func() (T1, T2)) func() (T1, T2)
OnceValues.text: OnceValues returns a function that invokes f only once and returns the values returned by f.

text/tabwriter.name: tabwriter
text/tabwriter.text: Package tabwriter implements a write filter (tabwriter.Writer) that translates tabbed columns in input into properly aligned text.

Writer.text: A Writer is a filter that inserts padding around tab-delimited columns in its input to align them in the output.

Flush.text: Flush should be called after the last call to Writer.Write to ensure that any data buffered in the Writer is written to output.

Init.decl: func (b *Writer) Init(output io.Writer, minwidth, tabwidth, padding int, padchar byte, flags uint) *Writer
Init.text: A Writer must be initialized with a call to Init.

Write.text: Write writes buf to the writer b.

NewWriter.decl: func NewWriter(output io.Writer, minwidth, tabwidth, padding int, padchar byte, flags uint) *Writer
NewWriter.text: NewWriter allocates and initializes a new Writer.

AlignRight.text: Formatting can be controlled with these flags.

Debug.text: Formatting can be controlled with these flags.

DiscardEmptyColumns.text: Formatting can be controlled with these flags.

Escape.text: To escape a text segment, bracket it with Escape characters.

FilterHTML.text: Formatting can be controlled with these flags.

StripEscape.text: Formatting can be controlled with these flags.

TabIndent.text: Formatting can be controlled with these flags.

time.name: time
time.text: Package time provides functionality for measuring and displaying time.

Duration.text: A Duration represents the elapsed time between two instants as an int64 nanosecond count.

Abs.text: Abs returns the absolute value of d.

Hours.text: Hours returns the duration as a floating point number of hours.

Microseconds.text: Microseconds returns the duration as an integer microsecond count.

Milliseconds.text: Milliseconds returns the duration as an integer millisecond count.

Minutes.text: Minutes returns the duration as a floating point number of minutes.

Nanoseconds.text: Nanoseconds returns the duration as an integer nanosecond count.

Round.text: Round returns the result of rounding d to the nearest multiple of m.

Seconds.text: Seconds returns the duration as a floating point number of seconds.

String.text: String returns a string representing the duration in the form "72h3m0.5s".

Truncate.text: Truncate returns the result of rounding d toward zero to a multiple of m.

Location.text: A Location maps time instants to the zone in use at that time.

String.text: String returns a descriptive name for the time zone information, corresponding to the name argument to LoadLocation or FixedZone.

Month.text: A Month specifies a month of the year (January = 1, ...).

String.text: String returns the English name of the month ("January", "February", ...).

ParseError.text: ParseError describes a problem parsing a time string.

Error.text: Error returns the string representation of a ParseError.

Ticker.text: A Ticker holds a channel that delivers “ticks” of a clock at intervals.

Reset.text: Reset stops a ticker and resets its period to the specified duration.

Time.text: A Time represents an instant in time with nanosecond precision.

AddDate.decl: func (t Time) AddDate(years int, months int, days int) Time
AddDate.text: AddDate returns the time corresponding to adding the given number of years, months, and days to t.

After.text: After reports whether the time instant t is after u.

AppendFormat.text: AppendFormat is like Time.Format but appends the textual representation to b and returns the extended buffer.

Before.text: Before reports whether the time instant t is before u.

Clock.decl: func (t Time) Clock() (hour, min, sec int)
Clock.text: Clock returns the hour, minute, and second within the day specified by t.

Compare.text: Compare compares the time instant t with u.

Date.decl: func (t Time) Date() (year int, month Month, day int)
Date.text: Date returns the year, month, and day in which t occurs.

Day.text: Day returns the day of the month specified by t.

Equal.text: Equal reports whether t and u represent the same time instant.

Format.text: Format returns a textual representation of the time value formatted according to the layout defined by the argument.

GoString.text: GoString implements fmt.GoStringer and formats t to be printed in Go source code.

Hour.text: Hour returns the hour within the day specified by t, in the range [0, 23].

ISOWeek.text: ISOWeek returns the ISO 8601 year and week number in which t occurs.

In.text: In returns a copy of t representing the same time instant, but with the copy's location information set to loc for display purposes.

IsDST.text: IsDST reports whether the time in the configured location is in Daylight Savings Time.

IsZero.text: IsZero reports whether t represents the zero time instant, January 1, year 1, 00:00:00 UTC.

Local.text: Local returns t with the location set to local time.

Location.text: Location returns the time zone information associated with t.

Minute.text: Minute returns the minute offset within the hour specified by t, in the range [0, 59].

Month.text: Month returns the month of the year specified by t.

Nanosecond.text: Nanosecond returns the nanosecond offset within the second specified by t, in the range [0, 999999999].

Round.text: Round returns the result of rounding t to the nearest multiple of d (since the zero time).

Second.text: Second returns the second offset within the minute specified by t, in the range [0, 59].

String.text: String returns the time formatted using the format string

Truncate.text: Truncate returns the result of rounding t down to a multiple of d (since the zero time).

UTC.text: UTC returns t with the location set to UTC.

Unix.text: Unix returns t as a Unix time, the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC.

UnixMicro.text: UnixMicro returns t as a Unix time, the number of microseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC.

UnixMilli.text: UnixMilli returns t as a Unix time, the number of milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC.

UnixNano.text: UnixNano returns t as a Unix time, the number of nanoseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC.

Weekday.text: Weekday returns the day of the week specified by t.

Year.text: Year returns the year in which t occurs.

YearDay.text: YearDay returns the day of the year specified by t, in the range [1,365] for non-leap years, and [1,366] in leap years.

Zone.decl: func (t Time) Zone() (name string, offset int)
Zone.text: Zone computes the time zone in effect at time t, returning the abbreviated name of the zone (such as "CET") and its offset in seconds east of UTC.

ZoneBounds.text: ZoneBounds returns the bounds of the time zone in effect at time t.

Timer.text: The Timer type represents a single event.

Reset.text: Reset changes the timer to expire after duration d.

Stop.text: Stop prevents the Timer from firing.

Weekday.text: A Weekday specifies a day of the week (Sunday = 0, ...).

String.text: String returns the English name of the day ("Sunday", "Monday", ...).

After.text: After waits for the duration to elapse and then sends the current time on the returned channel.

AfterFunc.text: AfterFunc waits for the duration to elapse and then calls f in its own goroutine.

Date.decl: func Date(year int, month Month, day, hour, min, sec, nsec int, loc *Location) Time
Date.text: Date returns the Time corresponding to

FixedZone.text: FixedZone returns a Location that always uses the given zone name and offset (seconds east of UTC).

LoadLocation.text: LoadLocation returns a Location with the given name.

LoadLocationFromTZData.text: LoadLocationFromTZData returns a new Location with the given name initialized from the IANA Time Zone database-formatted data.

NewTicker.text: NewTicker returns a new Ticker containing a channel that will send the current time on the channel after each tick.

NewTimer.text: NewTimer creates a new Timer that will send the current time on its channel after at least duration d.

Now.text: Now returns the current local time.

Parse.text: Parse parses a formatted string and returns the time value it represents.

ParseInLocation.decl: func ParseInLocation(layout, value string, loc *Location) (Time, error)
ParseInLocation.text: ParseInLocation is like Parse but differs in two important ways.

Since.text: Since returns the time elapsed since t.

Sleep.text: Sleep pauses the current goroutine for at least the duration d.

Tick.text: Tick is a convenience wrapper for NewTicker providing access to the ticking channel only.

Unix.decl: func Unix(sec int64, nsec int64) Time
Unix.text: Unix returns the local Time corresponding to the given Unix time, sec seconds and nsec nanoseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

UnixMicro.text: UnixMicro returns the local Time corresponding to the given Unix time, usec microseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

UnixMilli.text: UnixMilli returns the local Time corresponding to the given Unix time, msec milliseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

Until.text: Until returns the duration until t.

unicode.name: unicode
unicode.text: Package unicode provides data and functions to test some properties of Unicode code points.

CaseRange.text: CaseRange represents a range of Unicode code points for simple (one code point to one code point) case conversion.

Range16.text: Range16 represents of a range of 16-bit Unicode code points.

Range32.text: Range32 represents of a range of Unicode code points and is used when one or more of the values will not fit in 16 bits.

RangeTable.text: RangeTable defines a set of Unicode code points by listing the ranges of code points within the set.

SpecialCase.text: SpecialCase represents language-specific case mappings such as Turkish.

ToLower.text: ToLower maps the rune to lower case giving priority to the special mapping.

ToTitle.text: ToTitle maps the rune to title case giving priority to the special mapping.

ToUpper.text: ToUpper maps the rune to upper case giving priority to the special mapping.

In.text: In reports whether the rune is a member of one of the ranges.

Is.text: Is reports whether the rune is in the specified table of ranges.

IsControl.text: IsControl reports whether the rune is a control character.

IsDigit.text: IsDigit reports whether the rune is a decimal digit.

IsGraphic.text: IsGraphic reports whether the rune is defined as a Graphic by Unicode.

IsLetter.text: IsLetter reports whether the rune is a letter (category L).

IsLower.text: IsLower reports whether the rune is a lower case letter.

IsMark.text: IsMark reports whether the rune is a mark character (category M).

IsNumber.text: IsNumber reports whether the rune is a number (category N).

IsOneOf.text: IsOneOf reports whether the rune is a member of one of the ranges.

IsPrint.text: IsPrint reports whether the rune is defined as printable by Go.

IsPunct.text: IsPunct reports whether the rune is a Unicode punctuation character (category P).

IsSpace.text: IsSpace reports whether the rune is a space character as defined by Unicode's White Space property; in the Latin-1 space this is

IsSymbol.text: IsSymbol reports whether the rune is a symbolic character.

IsTitle.text: IsTitle reports whether the rune is a title case letter.

IsUpper.text: IsUpper reports whether the rune is an upper case letter.

SimpleFold.text: SimpleFold iterates over Unicode code points equivalent under the Unicode-defined simple case folding.

To.decl: func To(_case int, r rune) rune
To.text: To maps the rune to the specified case: UpperCase, LowerCase, or TitleCase.

ToLower.text: ToLower maps the rune to lower case.

ToTitle.text: ToTitle maps the rune to title case.

ToUpper.text: ToUpper maps the rune to upper case.

CaseRanges.text: CaseRanges is the table describing case mappings for all letters with non-self mappings.

Categories.text: Categories is the set of Unicode category tables.

CategoryAliases.text: CategoryAliases maps category aliases to standard category names.

FoldCategory.text: FoldCategory maps a category name to a table of code points outside the category that are equivalent under simple case folding to code points inside the category.

FoldScript.text: FoldScript maps a script name to a table of code points outside the script that are equivalent under simple case folding to code points inside the script.

GraphicRanges.text: GraphicRanges defines the set of graphic characters according to Unicode.

LowerCase.text: Indices into the Delta arrays inside CaseRanges for case mapping.

MaxCase.text: Indices into the Delta arrays inside CaseRanges for case mapping.

PrintRanges.text: PrintRanges defines the set of printable characters according to Go.

Properties.text: Properties is the set of Unicode property tables.

Scripts.text: Scripts is the set of Unicode script tables.

TitleCase.text: Indices into the Delta arrays inside CaseRanges for case mapping.

UpperCase.text: Indices into the Delta arrays inside CaseRanges for case mapping.

UpperLower.text: If the Delta field of a CaseRange is UpperLower, it means this CaseRange represents a sequence of the form (say) Upper Lower Upper Lower.

Version.text: Version is the Unicode edition from which the tables are derived.

unicode/utf8.name: utf8
unicode/utf8.text: Package utf8 implements functions and constants to support text encoded in UTF-8.

AppendRune.text: AppendRune appends the UTF-8 encoding of r to the end of p and returns the extended buffer.

DecodeLastRune.text: DecodeLastRune unpacks the last UTF-8 encoding in p and returns the rune and its width in bytes.

DecodeLastRuneInString.decl: func DecodeLastRuneInString(s string) (r rune, size int)
DecodeLastRuneInString.text: DecodeLastRuneInString is like DecodeLastRune but its input is a string.

DecodeRune.text: DecodeRune unpacks the first UTF-8 encoding in p and returns the rune and its width in bytes.

DecodeRuneInString.decl: func DecodeRuneInString(s string) (r rune, size int)
DecodeRuneInString.text: DecodeRuneInString is like DecodeRune but its input is a string.

EncodeRune.text: EncodeRune writes into p (which must be large enough) the UTF-8 encoding of the rune.

FullRune.text: FullRune reports whether the bytes in p begin with a full UTF-8 encoding of a rune.

FullRuneInString.text: FullRuneInString is like FullRune but its input is a string.

RuneCount.text: RuneCount returns the number of runes in p.

RuneCountInString.text: RuneCountInString is like RuneCount but its input is a string.

RuneLen.text: RuneLen returns the number of bytes in the UTF-8 encoding of the rune.

RuneStart.text: RuneStart reports whether the byte could be the first byte of an encoded, possibly invalid rune.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether p consists entirely of valid UTF-8-encoded runes.

ValidRune.text: ValidRune reports whether r can be legally encoded as UTF-8.

ValidString.text: ValidString reports whether s consists entirely of valid UTF-8-encoded runes.
